./AGENTS.md
```
 1  # Repository Guidelines
 2  
 3  ## Project Structure & Modules
 4  - Core package lives in `files_to_prompt/`: `cli.py` exposes the Click-based CLI, `__main__.py` enables `python -m files_to_prompt`, and `__init__.py` holds package metadata.
 5  - Tests sit in `tests/test_files_to_prompt.py`; keep new tests in this suite to mirror CLI behaviors.
 6  - Tooling and metadata are defined in `pyproject.toml`. Runtime dependency footprint is minimal (`click` only); avoid introducing new ones without discussion.
 7  
 8  ## Setup, Build, and Development Commands
 9  - Create an isolated environment: `python -m venv venv && source venv/bin/activate`.
10  - Install dependencies for local work: `pip install -e '.[test]'`.
11  - Run the CLI during development without installing globally: `python -m files_to_prompt path/to/dir -m` or `python -m files_to_prompt --help`.
12  - Package metadata is driven by `pyproject.toml`; bump versions there when preparing releases.
13  
14  ## Coding Style & Naming Conventions
15  - Follow standard Python 3.8+ conventions: 4-space indentation, snake_case for functions/variables, and meaningful, lowercase CLI option names.
16  - Keep functions small and reuse existing helpers (e.g., `process_path`, `print_as_markdown`) rather than adding branching in `cli()`.
17  - Prefer stdlib solutions; avoid new dependencies unless they deliver clear value.
18  - Match current import style (stdlib first, blank line, third-party).
19  
20  ## Testing Guidelines
21  - Primary test runner: `pytest`.
22  - Add or extend cases in `tests/test_files_to_prompt.py` when modifying CLI flags, output formats, or ignore rules.
23  - Include edge cases (hidden files, ignored paths, mixed encodings) and assert on concrete output strings, since the tool is output-centric.
24  - Run `pytest` before opening a PR; aim for coverage of new code paths rather than global percentage targets.
25  
26  ## Commit & Pull Request Guidelines
27  - Use concise, imperative commit subjects (e.g., `Add markdown line-number option`, `Refine ignore patterns`). One logical change per commit where possible.
28  - PRs should summarize intent, list main changes, and note testing performed (`pytest`). Link issues when they exist and include sample CLI output for user-facing changes.
29  - Keep diffs small and readable; prefer refactors in separate PRs from feature additions.
30  
31  ## Security & Configuration Tips
32  - The CLI reads files recursively; respect repository `.gitignore` handling and default hidden-file exclusion to avoid leaking secrets in prompts.
33  - When adding new options that affect file selection or output destinations, validate user inputs and maintain safe defaults (no overwriting unless requested).

./README.md
``````
  1  # files-to-prompt
  2  
  3  [![PyPI](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/files-to-prompt.svg)](https://pypi.org/project/files-to-prompt/)
  4  [![Changelog](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/simonw/files-to-prompt?include_prereleases&label=changelog)](https://github.com/simonw/files-to-prompt/releases)
  5  [![Tests](https://github.com/simonw/files-to-prompt/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/simonw/files-to-prompt/actions/workflows/test.yml)
  6  [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache%202.0-blue.svg)](https://github.com/simonw/files-to-prompt/blob/master/LICENSE)
  7  
  8  Concatenate a directory full of files into a single prompt for use with LLMs
  9  
 10  For background on this project see [Building files-to-prompt entirely using Claude 3 Opus](https://simonwillison.net/2024/Apr/8/files-to-prompt/).
 11  
 12  ## Installation
 13  
 14  Install this tool using `pip`:
 15  
 16  ```bash
 17  pip install files-to-prompt
 18  ```
 19  
 20  ## Usage
 21  
 22  To use `files-to-prompt`, provide the path to one or more files or directories you want to process:
 23  
 24  ```bash
 25  files-to-prompt path/to/file_or_directory [path/to/another/file_or_directory ...]
 26  ```
 27  
 28  This will output the contents of every file, with each file preceded by its relative path and separated by `---`.
 29  
 30  ### Options
 31  
 32  - `-e/--extension <extension>`: Only include files with the specified extension. Can be used multiple times.
 33  
 34    ```bash
 35    files-to-prompt path/to/directory -e txt -e md
 36    ```
 37  
 38  - `--include-hidden`: Include files and folders starting with `.` (hidden files and directories).
 39  
 40    ```bash
 41    files-to-prompt path/to/directory --include-hidden
 42    ```
 43  
 44  - `--ignore <pattern>`: Specify one or more patterns to ignore. Can be used multiple times. Patterns may match file names and directory names, unless you also specify `--ignore-files-only`. Pattern syntax uses [fnmatch](https://docs.python.org/3/library/fnmatch.html), which supports `*`, `?`, `[anychar]`, `[!notchars]` and `[?]` for special character literals.
 45    ```bash
 46    files-to-prompt path/to/directory --ignore "*.log" --ignore "temp*"
 47    ```
 48  
 49  - `--ignore-files-only`: Include directory paths which would otherwise be ignored by an `--ignore` pattern.
 50  
 51    ```bash
 52    files-to-prompt path/to/directory --ignore-files-only --ignore "*dir*"
 53    ```
 54  
 55  - `--ignore-gitignore`: Ignore `.gitignore` files and include all files.
 56  
 57    ```bash
 58    files-to-prompt path/to/directory --ignore-gitignore
 59    ```
 60  
 61  - `-c/--cxml`: Output in Claude XML format.
 62  
 63    ```bash
 64    files-to-prompt path/to/directory --cxml
 65    ```
 66  
 67  - `-m/--markdown`: Output as Markdown with fenced code blocks.
 68  
 69    ```bash
 70    files-to-prompt path/to/directory --markdown
 71    ```
 72  
 73  - `-o/--output <file>`: Write the output to a file instead of printing it to the console.
 74  
 75    ```bash
 76    files-to-prompt path/to/directory -o output.txt
 77    ```
 78  
 79  - `-n/--line-numbers`: Include line numbers in the output.
 80  
 81    ```bash
 82    files-to-prompt path/to/directory -n
 83    ```
 84    Example output:
 85    ```
 86    files_to_prompt/cli.py
 87    ---
 88      1  import os
 89      2  from fnmatch import fnmatch
 90      3
 91      4  import click
 92      ...
 93    ```
 94  
 95  - `-0/--null`: Use NUL character as separator when reading paths from stdin. Useful when filenames may contain spaces.
 96  
 97    ```bash
 98    find . -name "*.py" -print0 | files-to-prompt --null
 99    ```
100  
101  ### Example
102  
103  Suppose you have a directory structure like this:
104  
105  ```
106  my_directory/
107  ├── file1.txt
108  ├── file2.txt
109  ├── .hidden_file.txt
110  ├── temp.log
111  └── subdirectory/
112      └── file3.txt
113  ```
114  
115  Running `files-to-prompt my_directory` will output:
116  
117  ```
118  my_directory/file1.txt
119  ---
120  Contents of file1.txt
121  ---
122  my_directory/file2.txt
123  ---
124  Contents of file2.txt
125  ---
126  my_directory/subdirectory/file3.txt
127  ---
128  Contents of file3.txt
129  ---
130  ```
131  
132  If you run `files-to-prompt my_directory --include-hidden`, the output will also include `.hidden_file.txt`:
133  
134  ```
135  my_directory/.hidden_file.txt
136  ---
137  Contents of .hidden_file.txt
138  ---
139  ...
140  ```
141  
142  If you run `files-to-prompt my_directory --ignore "*.log"`, the output will exclude `temp.log`:
143  
144  ```
145  my_directory/file1.txt
146  ---
147  Contents of file1.txt
148  ---
149  my_directory/file2.txt
150  ---
151  Contents of file2.txt
152  ---
153  my_directory/subdirectory/file3.txt
154  ---
155  Contents of file3.txt
156  ---
157  ```
158  
159  If you run `files-to-prompt my_directory --ignore "sub*"`, the output will exclude all files in `subdirectory/` (unless you also specify `--ignore-files-only`):
160  
161  ```
162  my_directory/file1.txt
163  ---
164  Contents of file1.txt
165  ---
166  my_directory/file2.txt
167  ---
168  Contents of file2.txt
169  ---
170  ```
171  
172  ### Reading from stdin
173  
174  The tool can also read paths from standard input. This can be used to pipe in the output of another command:
175  
176  ```bash
177  # Find files modified in the last day
178  find . -mtime -1 | files-to-prompt
179  ```
180  
181  When using the `--null` (or `-0`) option, paths are expected to be NUL-separated (useful when dealing with filenames containing spaces):
182  
183  ```bash
184  find . -name "*.txt" -print0 | files-to-prompt --null
185  ```
186  
187  You can mix and match paths from command line arguments and stdin:
188  
189  ```bash
190  # Include files modified in the last day, and also include README.md
191  find . -mtime -1 | files-to-prompt README.md
192  ```
193  
194  ### Claude XML Output
195  
196  Anthropic has provided [specific guidelines](https://docs.anthropic.com/claude/docs/long-context-window-tips) for optimally structuring prompts to take advantage of Claude's extended context window.
197  
198  To structure the output in this way, use the optional `--cxml` flag, which will produce output like this:
199  
200  ```xml
201  <documents>
202  <document index="1">
203  <source>my_directory/file1.txt</source>
204  <document_content>
205  Contents of file1.txt
206  </document_content>
207  </document>
208  <document index="2">
209  <source>my_directory/file2.txt</source>
210  <document_content>
211  Contents of file2.txt
212  </document_content>
213  </document>
214  </documents>
215  ```
216  
217  ## --markdown fenced code block output
218  
219  The `--markdown` option will output the files as fenced code blocks, which can be useful for pasting into Markdown documents.
220  
221  ```bash
222  files-to-prompt path/to/directory --markdown
223  ```
224  The language tag will be guessed based on the filename.
225  
226  If the code itself contains triple backticks the wrapper around it will use one additional backtick.
227  
228  Example output:
229  `````
230  myfile.py
231  ```python
232  def my_function():
233      return "Hello, world!"
234  ```
235  other.js
236  ```javascript
237  function myFunction() {
238      return "Hello, world!";
239  }
240  ```
241  file_with_triple_backticks.md
242  ````markdown
243  This file has its own
244  ```
245  fenced code blocks
246  ```
247  Inside it.
248  ````
249  `````
250  
251  ## Development
252  
253  To contribute to this tool, first checkout the code. Then create a new virtual environment:
254  
255  ```bash
256  cd files-to-prompt
257  python -m venv venv
258  source venv/bin/activate
259  ```
260  
261  Now install the dependencies and test dependencies:
262  
263  ```bash
264  pip install -e '.[test]'
265  ```
266  
267  To run the tests:
268  
269  ```bash
270  pytest
271  ```
``````

  1  import os
  2  import sys
  3  import subprocess
  4  from fnmatch import fnmatch
  5  
  6  import click
  7  
  8  global_index = 1
  9  
 10  EXT_TO_LANG = {
 11      "py": "python",
 12      "c": "c",
 13      "cpp": "cpp",
 14      "java": "java",
 15      "js": "javascript",
 16      "ts": "typescript",
 17      "html": "html",
 18      "css": "css",
 19      "xml": "xml",
 20      "json": "json",
 21      "yaml": "yaml",
 22      "yml": "yaml",
 23      "sh": "bash",
 24      "rb": "ruby",
 25  }
 26  
 27  
 28  def should_ignore(path, gitignore_rules):
 29      for rule in gitignore_rules:
 30          if fnmatch(os.path.basename(path), rule):
 31              return True
 32          if os.path.isdir(path) and fnmatch(os.path.basename(path) + "/", rule):
 33              return True
 34      return False
 35  
 36  
 37  def read_gitignore(path):
 38      gitignore_path = os.path.join(path, ".gitignore")
 39      if os.path.isfile(gitignore_path):
 40          with open(gitignore_path, "r") as f:
 41              return [
 42                  line.strip() for line in f if line.strip() and not line.startswith("#")
 43              ]
 44      return []
 45  
 46  
 47  def add_line_numbers(content):
 48      lines = content.splitlines()
 49  
 50      padding = len(str(len(lines)))
 51  
 52      numbered_lines = [f"{i + 1:{padding}}  {line}" for i, line in enumerate(lines)]
 53      return "\n".join(numbered_lines)
 54  
 55  
 56  def extract_docx_text(file_path):
 57      """Extract text from a DOCX file using pandoc."""
 58      try:
 59          # Use pandoc to convert DOCX to markdown with tracked changes
 60          result = subprocess.run(
 61              ["pandoc", "--track-changes=all", file_path, "-t", "markdown"],
 62              capture_output=True,
 63              text=True,
 64              check=True,
 65          )
 66          return result.stdout
 67      except subprocess.CalledProcessError as e:
 68          warning_message = (
 69              f"Warning: Failed to extract text from {file_path} using pandoc: {e.stderr}"
 70          )
 71          click.echo(click.style(warning_message, fg="red"), err=True)
 72          return ""
 73      except FileNotFoundError:
 74          warning_message = f"Warning: pandoc not found. Please install pandoc to extract text from DOCX files."
 75          click.echo(click.style(warning_message, fg="red"), err=True)
 76          return ""
 77  
 78  
 79  def extract_pdf_text(file_path):
 80      """Extract text and tables from a PDF file using pdfplumber."""
 81      try:
 82          import pdfplumber
 83      except ImportError:
 84          warning_message = f"Warning: pdfplumber not installed. Please install pdfplumber to extract text from PDF files."
 85          click.echo(click.style(warning_message, fg="red"), err=True)
 86          return ""
 87  
 88      content_parts = []
 89      try:
 90          with pdfplumber.open(file_path) as pdf:
 91              for i, page in enumerate(pdf.pages):
 92                  # Extract text
 93                  text = page.extract_text()
 94                  if text:
 95                      content_parts.append(text)
 96  
 97                  # Extract tables
 98                  tables = page.extract_tables()
 99                  if tables:
100                      for j, table in enumerate(tables):
101                          if table:
102                              content_parts.append(f"\n\nTable {j+1} on page {i+1}:\n")
103                              # Format table as markdown
104                              markdown_table = format_table_as_markdown(table)
105                              content_parts.append(markdown_table)
106  
107          return "\n".join(content_parts)
108      except Exception as e:
109          warning_message = f"Warning: Failed to extract text from {file_path}: {str(e)}"
110          click.echo(click.style(warning_message, fg="red"), err=True)
111          return ""
112  
113  
114  def format_table_as_markdown(table):
115      """Format a table (list of lists) as markdown table."""
116      if not table or not table[0]:
117          return ""
118  
119      # Find the maximum number of columns across all rows
120      max_cols = max(len(row) for row in table if row)
121  
122      markdown_lines = []
123      # Header row
124      header = table[0]
125      # Pad header to max_cols if needed
126      header_padded = list(header) + [""] * (max_cols - len(header))
127      markdown_lines.append(
128          "| " + " | ".join(str(cell) if cell else "" for cell in header_padded) + " |"
129      )
130      markdown_lines.append("| " + " | ".join("---" for _ in range(max_cols)) + " |")
131  
132      # Data rows
133      for row in table[1:]:
134          # Pad row to max_cols if needed
135          row_padded = list(row) + [""] * (max_cols - len(row))
136          markdown_lines.append(
137              "| " + " | ".join(str(cell) if cell else "" for cell in row_padded) + " |"
138          )
139  
140      return "\n".join(markdown_lines)
141  
142  
143  def read_file_content(file_path):
144      """Read file content, handling different file types."""
145      file_ext = os.path.splitext(file_path)[1].lower()
146  
147      if file_ext == ".docx":
148          return extract_docx_text(file_path)
149      elif file_ext == ".pdf":
150          return extract_pdf_text(file_path)
151      else:
152          # Default: read as text
153          # Try UTF-8 first, then raise UnicodeDecodeError if it fails
154          # This preserves the original behavior for binary files
155          with open(file_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
156              return f.read()
157  
158  
159  def print_path(writer, path, content, cxml, markdown, line_numbers):
160      if cxml:
161          print_as_xml(writer, path, content, line_numbers)
162      elif markdown:
163          print_as_markdown(writer, path, content, line_numbers)
164      else:
165          print_default(writer, path, content, line_numbers)
166  
167  
168  def print_default(writer, path, content, line_numbers):
169      writer(path)
170      writer("---")
171      if line_numbers:
172          content = add_line_numbers(content)
173      writer(content)
174      writer("")
175      writer("---")
176  
177  
178  def print_as_xml(writer, path, content, line_numbers):
179      global global_index
180      writer(f'<document index="{global_index}">')
181      writer(f"<source>{path}</source>")
182      writer("<document_content>")
183      if line_numbers:
184          content = add_line_numbers(content)
185      writer(content)
186      writer("</document_content>")
187      writer("</document>")
188      global_index += 1
189  
190  
191  def print_as_markdown(writer, path, content, line_numbers):
192      lang = EXT_TO_LANG.get(path.split(".")[-1], "")
193      # Figure out how many backticks to use
194      backticks = "```"
195      while backticks in content:
196          backticks += "`"
197      writer(path)
198      writer(f"{backticks}{lang}")
199      if line_numbers:
200          content = add_line_numbers(content)
201      writer(content)
202      writer(f"{backticks}")
203  
204  
205  def process_path(
206      path,
207      extensions,
208      include_hidden,
209      ignore_files_only,
210      ignore_gitignore,
211      gitignore_rules,
212      ignore_patterns,
213      writer,
214      claude_xml,
215      markdown,
216      line_numbers=False,
217  ):
218      if os.path.isfile(path):
219          try:
220              content = read_file_content(path)
221              print_path(writer, path, content, claude_xml, markdown, line_numbers)
222          except UnicodeDecodeError:
223              warning_message = f"Warning: Skipping file {path} due to UnicodeDecodeError"
224              click.echo(click.style(warning_message, fg="red"), err=True)
225          except Exception as e:
226              warning_message = f"Warning: Skipping file {path} due to error: {str(e)}"
227              click.echo(click.style(warning_message, fg="red"), err=True)
228      elif os.path.isdir(path):
229          for root, dirs, files in os.walk(path):
230              if not include_hidden:
231                  dirs[:] = [d for d in dirs if not d.startswith(".")]
232                  files = [f for f in files if not f.startswith(".")]
233  
234              if not ignore_gitignore:
235                  gitignore_rules.extend(read_gitignore(root))
236                  dirs[:] = [
237                      d
238                      for d in dirs
239                      if not should_ignore(os.path.join(root, d), gitignore_rules)
240                  ]
241                  files = [
242                      f
243                      for f in files
244                      if not should_ignore(os.path.join(root, f), gitignore_rules)
245                  ]
246  
247              if ignore_patterns:
248                  if not ignore_files_only:
249                      dirs[:] = [
250                          d
251                          for d in dirs
252                          if not any(fnmatch(d, pattern) for pattern in ignore_patterns)
253                      ]
254                  files = [
255                      f
256                      for f in files
257                      if not any(fnmatch(f, pattern) for pattern in ignore_patterns)
258                  ]
259  
260              if extensions:
261                  files = [f for f in files if f.endswith(extensions)]
262  
263              for file in sorted(files):
264                  file_path = os.path.join(root, file)
265                  try:
266                      content = read_file_content(file_path)
267                      print_path(
268                          writer,
269                          file_path,
270                          content,
271                          claude_xml,
272                          markdown,
273                          line_numbers,
274                      )
275                  except UnicodeDecodeError:
276                      warning_message = (
277                          f"Warning: Skipping file {file_path} due to UnicodeDecodeError"
278                      )
279                      click.echo(click.style(warning_message, fg="red"), err=True)
280                  except Exception as e:
281                      warning_message = (
282                          f"Warning: Skipping file {file_path} due to error: {str(e)}"
283                      )
284                      click.echo(click.style(warning_message, fg="red"), err=True)
285  
286  
287  def read_paths_from_stdin(use_null_separator):
288      if sys.stdin.isatty():
289          # No ready input from stdin, don't block for input
290          return []
291  
292      stdin_content = sys.stdin.read()
293      if use_null_separator:
294          paths = stdin_content.split("\0")
295      else:
296          paths = stdin_content.split()  # split on whitespace
297      return [p for p in paths if p]
298  
299  
300  @click.command()
301  @click.argument("paths", nargs=-1, type=click.Path(exists=True))
302  @click.option("extensions", "-e", "--extension", multiple=True)
303  @click.option(
304      "--include-hidden",
305      is_flag=True,
306      help="Include files and folders starting with .",
307  )
308  @click.option(
309      "--ignore-files-only",
310      is_flag=True,
311      help="--ignore option only ignores files",
312  )
313  @click.option(
314      "--ignore-gitignore",
315      is_flag=True,
316      help="Ignore .gitignore files and include all files",
317  )
318  @click.option(
319      "ignore_patterns",
320      "--ignore",
321      multiple=True,
322      default=[],
323      help="List of patterns to ignore",
324  )
325  @click.option(
326      "output_file",
327      "-o",
328      "--output",
329      type=click.Path(writable=True),
330      help="Output to a file instead of stdout",
331  )
332  @click.option(
333      "claude_xml",
334      "-c",
335      "--cxml",
336      is_flag=True,
337      help="Output in XML-ish format suitable for Claude's long context window.",
338  )
339  @click.option(
340      "markdown",
341      "-m",
342      "--markdown",
343      is_flag=True,
344      help="Output Markdown with fenced code blocks",
345  )
346  @click.option(
347      "line_numbers",
348      "-n",
349      "--line-numbers",
350      is_flag=True,
351      help="Add line numbers to the output",
352  )
353  @click.option(
354      "--null",
355      "-0",
356      is_flag=True,
357      help="Use NUL character as separator when reading from stdin",
358  )
359  @click.version_option()
360  def cli(
361      paths,
362      extensions,
363      include_hidden,
364      ignore_files_only,
365      ignore_gitignore,
366      ignore_patterns,
367      output_file,
368      claude_xml,
369      markdown,
370      line_numbers,
371      null,
372  ):
373      """
374      Takes one or more paths to files or directories and outputs every file,
375      recursively, each one preceded with its filename like this:
376  
377      \b
378          path/to/file.py
379          ----
380          Contents of file.py goes here
381          ---
382          path/to/file2.py
383          ---
384          ...
385  
386      If the `--cxml` flag is provided, the output will be structured as follows:
387  
388      \b
389          <documents>
390          <document path="path/to/file1.txt">
391          Contents of file1.txt
392          </document>
393          <document path="path/to/file2.txt">
394          Contents of file2.txt
395          </document>
396          ...
397          </documents>
398  
399      If the `--markdown` flag is provided, the output will be structured as follows:
400  
401      \b
402          path/to/file1.py
403          ```python
404          Contents of file1.py
405          ```
406      """
407      # Reset global_index for pytest
408      global global_index
409      global_index = 1
410  
411      # Read paths from stdin if available
412      stdin_paths = read_paths_from_stdin(use_null_separator=null)
413  
414      # Combine paths from arguments and stdin
415      paths = [*paths, *stdin_paths]
416  
417      gitignore_rules = []
418      writer = click.echo
419      fp = None
420      if output_file:
421          fp = open(output_file, "w", encoding="utf-8")
422          writer = lambda s: print(s, file=fp)
423      for path in paths:
424          if not os.path.exists(path):
425              raise click.BadArgumentUsage(f"Path does not exist: {path}")
426          if not ignore_gitignore:
427              gitignore_rules.extend(read_gitignore(os.path.dirname(path)))
428          if claude_xml and path == paths[0]:
429              writer("<documents>")
430          process_path(
431              path,
432              extensions,
433              include_hidden,
434              ignore_files_only,
435              ignore_gitignore,
436              gitignore_rules,
437              ignore_patterns,
438              writer,
439              claude_xml,
440              markdown,
441              line_numbers,
442          )
443      if claude_xml:
444          writer("</documents>")
445      if fp:
446          fp.close()

444  def test_docx_extraction():
445      """Test that DOCX files can be extracted and processed."""
446      runner = CliRunner()
447      # Use the sample DOCX file from tests/media
448      docx_path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "media", "Gemini 3 Developer Guide.docx")
449      
450      if not os.path.exists(docx_path):
451          pytest.skip(f"Sample DOCX file not found at {docx_path}")
452      
453      result = runner.invoke(cli, [docx_path])
454      assert result.exit_code == 0
455      assert docx_path in result.output
456      # Check that some content was extracted (not empty)
457      # The exact content depends on the file, but we should have more than just the path
458      output_lines = result.output.split("\n")
459      content_lines = [line for line in output_lines if line.strip() and not line.startswith("---") and docx_path not in line]
460      assert len(content_lines) > 0, "DOCX file should have extracted content"

   1  ./AGENTS.md
   2  ```
   3   1  # Repository Guidelines
   4   2  
   5   3  ## Project Structure & Modules
   6   4  - Core package lives in `files_to_prompt/`: `cli.py` exposes the Click-based CLI, `__main__.py` enables `python -m files_to_prompt`, and `__init__.py` holds package metadata.
   7   5  - Tests sit in `tests/test_files_to_prompt.py`; keep new tests in this suite to mirror CLI behaviors.
   8   6  - Tooling and metadata are defined in `pyproject.toml`. Runtime dependency footprint is minimal (`click` only); avoid introducing new ones without discussion.
   9   7  
  10   8  ## Setup, Build, and Development Commands
  11   9  - Create an isolated environment: `python -m venv venv && source venv/bin/activate`.
  12  10  - Install dependencies for local work: `pip install -e '.[test]'`.
  13  11  - Run the CLI during development without installing globally: `python -m files_to_prompt path/to/dir -m` or `python -m files_to_prompt --help`.
  14  12  - Package metadata is driven by `pyproject.toml`; bump versions there when preparing releases.
  15  13  
  16  14  ## Coding Style & Naming Conventions
  17  15  - Follow standard Python 3.8+ conventions: 4-space indentation, snake_case for functions/variables, and meaningful, lowercase CLI option names.
  18  16  - Keep functions small and reuse existing helpers (e.g., `process_path`, `print_as_markdown`) rather than adding branching in `cli()`.
  19  17  - Prefer stdlib solutions; avoid new dependencies unless they deliver clear value.
  20  18  - Match current import style (stdlib first, blank line, third-party).
  21  19  
  22  20  ## Testing Guidelines
  23  21  - Primary test runner: `pytest`.
  24  22  - Add or extend cases in `tests/test_files_to_prompt.py` when modifying CLI flags, output formats, or ignore rules.
  25  23  - Include edge cases (hidden files, ignored paths, mixed encodings) and assert on concrete output strings, since the tool is output-centric.
  26  24  - Run `pytest` before opening a PR; aim for coverage of new code paths rather than global percentage targets.
  27  25  
  28  26  ## Commit & Pull Request Guidelines
  29  27  - Use concise, imperative commit subjects (e.g., `Add markdown line-number option`, `Refine ignore patterns`). One logical change per commit where possible.
  30  28  - PRs should summarize intent, list main changes, and note testing performed (`pytest`). Link issues when they exist and include sample CLI output for user-facing changes.
  31  29  - Keep diffs small and readable; prefer refactors in separate PRs from feature additions.
  32  30  
  33  31  ## Security & Configuration Tips
  34  32  - The CLI reads files recursively; respect repository `.gitignore` handling and default hidden-file exclusion to avoid leaking secrets in prompts.
  35  33  - When adding new options that affect file selection or output destinations, validate user inputs and maintain safe defaults (no overwriting unless requested).
  36  ```
  37  ./README.md
  38  ``````
  39    1  # files-to-prompt
  40    2  
  41    3  [![PyPI](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/files-to-prompt.svg)](https://pypi.org/project/files-to-prompt/)
  42    4  [![Changelog](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/simonw/files-to-prompt?include_prereleases&label=changelog)](https://github.com/simonw/files-to-prompt/releases)
  43    5  [![Tests](https://github.com/simonw/files-to-prompt/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/simonw/files-to-prompt/actions/workflows/test.yml)
  44    6  [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache%202.0-blue.svg)](https://github.com/simonw/files-to-prompt/blob/master/LICENSE)
  45    7  
  46    8  Concatenate a directory full of files into a single prompt for use with LLMs
  47    9  
  48   10  For background on this project see [Building files-to-prompt entirely using Claude 3 Opus](https://simonwillison.net/2024/Apr/8/files-to-prompt/).
  49   11  
  50   12  ## Installation
  51   13  
  52   14  Install this tool using `pip`:
  53   15  
  54   16  ```bash
  55   17  pip install files-to-prompt
  56   18  ```
  57   19  
  58   20  ## Usage
  59   21  
  60   22  To use `files-to-prompt`, provide the path to one or more files or directories you want to process:
  61   23  
  62   24  ```bash
  63   25  files-to-prompt path/to/file_or_directory [path/to/another/file_or_directory ...]
  64   26  ```
  65   27  
  66   28  This will output the contents of every file, with each file preceded by its relative path and separated by `---`.
  67   29  
  68   30  ### Options
  69   31  
  70   32  - `-e/--extension <extension>`: Only include files with the specified extension. Can be used multiple times.
  71   33  
  72   34    ```bash
  73   35    files-to-prompt path/to/directory -e txt -e md
  74   36    ```
  75   37  
  76   38  - `--include-hidden`: Include files and folders starting with `.` (hidden files and directories).
  77   39  
  78   40    ```bash
  79   41    files-to-prompt path/to/directory --include-hidden
  80   42    ```
  81   43  
  82   44  - `--ignore <pattern>`: Specify one or more patterns to ignore. Can be used multiple times. Patterns may match file names and directory names, unless you also specify `--ignore-files-only`. Pattern syntax uses [fnmatch](https://docs.python.org/3/library/fnmatch.html), which supports `*`, `?`, `[anychar]`, `[!notchars]` and `[?]` for special character literals.
  83   45    ```bash
  84   46    files-to-prompt path/to/directory --ignore "*.log" --ignore "temp*"
  85   47    ```
  86   48  
  87   49  - `--ignore-files-only`: Include directory paths which would otherwise be ignored by an `--ignore` pattern.
  88   50  
  89   51    ```bash
  90   52    files-to-prompt path/to/directory --ignore-files-only --ignore "*dir*"
  91   53    ```
  92   54  
  93   55  - `--ignore-gitignore`: Ignore `.gitignore` files and include all files.
  94   56  
  95   57    ```bash
  96   58    files-to-prompt path/to/directory --ignore-gitignore
  97   59    ```
  98   60  
  99   61  - `-c/--cxml`: Output in Claude XML format.
 100   62  
 101   63    ```bash
 102   64    files-to-prompt path/to/directory --cxml
 103   65    ```
 104   66  
 105   67  - `-m/--markdown`: Output as Markdown with fenced code blocks.
 106   68  
 107   69    ```bash
 108   70    files-to-prompt path/to/directory --markdown
 109   71    ```
 110   72  
 111   73  - `-o/--output <file>`: Write the output to a file instead of printing it to the console.
 112   74  
 113   75    ```bash
 114   76    files-to-prompt path/to/directory -o output.txt
 115   77    ```
 116   78  
 117   79  - `-n/--line-numbers`: Include line numbers in the output.
 118   80  
 119   81    ```bash
 120   82    files-to-prompt path/to/directory -n
 121   83    ```
 122   84    Example output:
 123   85    ```
 124   86    files_to_prompt/cli.py
 125   87    ---
 126   88      1  import os
 127   89      2  from fnmatch import fnmatch
 128   90      3
 129   91      4  import click
 130   92      ...
 131   93    ```
 132   94  
 133   95  - `-0/--null`: Use NUL character as separator when reading paths from stdin. Useful when filenames may contain spaces.
 134   96  
 135   97    ```bash
 136   98    find . -name "*.py" -print0 | files-to-prompt --null
 137   99    ```
 138  100  
 139  101  ### Example
 140  102  
 141  103  Suppose you have a directory structure like this:
 142  104  
 143  105  ```
 144  106  my_directory/
 145  107  ├── file1.txt
 146  108  ├── file2.txt
 147  109  ├── .hidden_file.txt
 148  110  ├── temp.log
 149  111  └── subdirectory/
 150  112      └── file3.txt
 151  113  ```
 152  114  
 153  115  Running `files-to-prompt my_directory` will output:
 154  116  
 155  117  ```
 156  118  my_directory/file1.txt
 157  119  ---
 158  120  Contents of file1.txt
 159  121  ---
 160  122  my_directory/file2.txt
 161  123  ---
 162  124  Contents of file2.txt
 163  125  ---
 164  126  my_directory/subdirectory/file3.txt
 165  127  ---
 166  128  Contents of file3.txt
 167  129  ---
 168  130  ```
 169  131  
 170  132  If you run `files-to-prompt my_directory --include-hidden`, the output will also include `.hidden_file.txt`:
 171  133  
 172  134  ```
 173  135  my_directory/.hidden_file.txt
 174  136  ---
 175  137  Contents of .hidden_file.txt
 176  138  ---
 177  139  ...
 178  140  ```
 179  141  
 180  142  If you run `files-to-prompt my_directory --ignore "*.log"`, the output will exclude `temp.log`:
 181  143  
 182  144  ```
 183  145  my_directory/file1.txt
 184  146  ---
 185  147  Contents of file1.txt
 186  148  ---
 187  149  my_directory/file2.txt
 188  150  ---
 189  151  Contents of file2.txt
 190  152  ---
 191  153  my_directory/subdirectory/file3.txt
 192  154  ---
 193  155  Contents of file3.txt
 194  156  ---
 195  157  ```
 196  158  
 197  159  If you run `files-to-prompt my_directory --ignore "sub*"`, the output will exclude all files in `subdirectory/` (unless you also specify `--ignore-files-only`):
 198  160  
 199  161  ```
 200  162  my_directory/file1.txt
 201  163  ---
 202  164  Contents of file1.txt
 203  165  ---
 204  166  my_directory/file2.txt
 205  167  ---
 206  168  Contents of file2.txt
 207  169  ---
 208  170  ```
 209  171  
 210  172  ### Reading from stdin
 211  173  
 212  174  The tool can also read paths from standard input. This can be used to pipe in the output of another command:
 213  175  
 214  176  ```bash
 215  177  # Find files modified in the last day
 216  178  find . -mtime -1 | files-to-prompt
 217  179  ```
 218  180  
 219  181  When using the `--null` (or `-0`) option, paths are expected to be NUL-separated (useful when dealing with filenames containing spaces):
 220  182  
 221  183  ```bash
 222  184  find . -name "*.txt" -print0 | files-to-prompt --null
 223  185  ```
 224  186  
 225  187  You can mix and match paths from command line arguments and stdin:
 226  188  
 227  189  ```bash
 228  190  # Include files modified in the last day, and also include README.md
 229  191  find . -mtime -1 | files-to-prompt README.md
 230  192  ```
 231  193  
 232  194  ### Claude XML Output
 233  195  
 234  196  Anthropic has provided [specific guidelines](https://docs.anthropic.com/claude/docs/long-context-window-tips) for optimally structuring prompts to take advantage of Claude's extended context window.
 235  197  
 236  198  To structure the output in this way, use the optional `--cxml` flag, which will produce output like this:
 237  199  
 238  200  ```xml
 239  201  <documents>
 240  202  <document index="1">
 241  203  <source>my_directory/file1.txt</source>
 242  204  <document_content>
 243  205  Contents of file1.txt
 244  206  </document_content>
 245  207  </document>
 246  208  <document index="2">
 247  209  <source>my_directory/file2.txt</source>
 248  210  <document_content>
 249  211  Contents of file2.txt
 250  212  </document_content>
 251  213  </document>
 252  214  </documents>
 253  215  ```
 254  216  
 255  217  ## --markdown fenced code block output
 256  218  
 257  219  The `--markdown` option will output the files as fenced code blocks, which can be useful for pasting into Markdown documents.
 258  220  
 259  221  ```bash
 260  222  files-to-prompt path/to/directory --markdown
 261  223  ```
 262  224  The language tag will be guessed based on the filename.
 263  225  
 264  226  If the code itself contains triple backticks the wrapper around it will use one additional backtick.
 265  227  
 266  228  Example output:
 267  229  `````
 268  230  myfile.py
 269  231  ```python
 270  232  def my_function():
 271  233      return "Hello, world!"
 272  234  ```
 273  235  other.js
 274  236  ```javascript
 275  237  function myFunction() {
 276  238      return "Hello, world!";
 277  239  }
 278  240  ```
 279  241  file_with_triple_backticks.md
 280  242  ````markdown
 281  243  This file has its own
 282  244  ```
 283  245  fenced code blocks
 284  246  ```
 285  247  Inside it.
 286  248  ````
 287  249  `````
 288  250  
 289  251  ## Development
 290  252  
 291  253  To contribute to this tool, first checkout the code. Then create a new virtual environment:
 292  254  
 293  255  ```bash
 294  256  cd files-to-prompt
 295  257  python -m venv venv
 296  258  source venv/bin/activate
 297  259  ```
 298  260  
 299  261  Now install the dependencies and test dependencies:
 300  262  
 301  263  ```bash
 302  264  pip install -e '.[test]'
 303  265  ```
 304  266  
 305  267  To run the tests:
 306  268  
 307  269  ```bash
 308  270  pytest
 309  271  ```

1449   28  def should_ignore(path, gitignore_rules):
1450   29      for rule in gitignore_rules:
1451   30          if fnmatch(os.path.basename(path), rule):
1452   31              return True
1453   32          if os.path.isdir(path) and fnmatch(os.path.basename(path) + "/", rule):
1454   33              return True
1455   34      return False

1458   37  def read_gitignore(path):
1459   38      gitignore_path = os.path.join(path, ".gitignore")
1460   39      if os.path.isfile(gitignore_path):
1461   40          with open(gitignore_path, "r") as f:
1462   41              return [
1463   42                  line.strip() for line in f if line.strip() and not line.startswith("#")
1464   43              ]

1468   47  def add_line_numbers(content):
1469   48      lines = content.splitlines()
1470   49  
1471   50      padding = len(str(len(lines)))
1472   51  
1473   52      numbered_lines = [f"{i + 1:{padding}}  {line}" for i, line in enumerate(lines)]
1474   53      return "\n".join(numbered_lines)

1477   56  def extract_docx_text(file_path):
1478   57      """Extract text from a DOCX file using pandoc."""
1479   58      try:
1480   59          # Use pandoc to convert DOCX to markdown with tracked changes
1481   60          result = subprocess.run(
1482   61              ["pandoc", "--track-changes=all", file_path, "-t", "markdown"],
1483   62              capture_output=True,
1484   63              text=True,
1485   64              check=True,
1486   65          )
1487   66          return result.stdout
1488   67      except subprocess.CalledProcessError as e:
1489   68          warning_message = (
1490   69              f"Warning: Failed to extract text from {file_path} using pandoc: {e.stderr}"
1491   70          )
1492   71          click.echo(click.style(warning_message, fg="red"), err=True)
1493   72          return ""
1494   73      except FileNotFoundError:
1495   74          warning_message = f"Warning: pandoc not found. Please install pandoc to extract text from DOCX files."
1496   75          click.echo(click.style(warning_message, fg="red"), err=True)
1497   76          return ""
1498   77  
1499   78  
1500   79  def extract_pdf_text(file_path):
1501   80      """Extract text and tables from a PDF file using pdfplumber."""
1502   81      try:
1503   82          import pdfplumber
1504   83      except ImportError:
1505   84          warning_message = f"Warning: pdfplumber not installed. Please install pdfplumber to extract text from PDF files."
1506   85          click.echo(click.style(warning_message, fg="red"), err=True)
1507   86          return ""
1508   87  
1509   88      content_parts = []
1510   89      try:
1511   90          with pdfplumber.open(file_path) as pdf:
1512   91              for i, page in enumerate(pdf.pages):
1513   92                  # Extract text
1514   93                  text = page.extract_text()
1515   94                  if text:
1516   95                      content_parts.append(text)
1517   96  
1518   97                  # Extract tables
1519   98                  tables = page.extract_tables()
1520   99                  if tables:
1521  100                      for j, table in enumerate(tables):
1522  101                          if table:
1523  102                              content_parts.append(f"\n\nTable {j+1} on page {i+1}:\n")
1524  103                              # Format table as markdown
1525  104                              markdown_table = format_table_as_markdown(table)
1526  105                              content_parts.append(markdown_table)
1527  106  
1528  107          return "\n".join(content_parts)
1529  108      except Exception as e:
1530  109          warning_message = f"Warning: Failed to extract text from {file_path}: {str(e)}"
1531  110          click.echo(click.style(warning_message, fg="red"), err=True)
1532  111          return ""
1533  112  
1534  113  
1535  114  def format_table_as_markdown(table):
1536  115      """Format a table (list of lists) as markdown table."""
1537  116      if not table or not table[0]:
1538  117          return ""
1539  118  
1540  119      # Find the maximum number of columns across all rows
1541  120      max_cols = max(len(row) for row in table if row)
1542  121  
1543  122      markdown_lines = []
1544  123      # Header row
1545  124      header = table[0]
1546  125      # Pad header to max_cols if needed
1547  126      header_padded = list(header) + [""] * (max_cols - len(header))
1548  127      markdown_lines.append(
1549  128          "| " + " | ".join(str(cell) if cell else "" for cell in header_padded) + " |"
1550  129      )
1551  130      markdown_lines.append("| " + " | ".join("---" for _ in range(max_cols)) + " |")
1552  131  
1553  132      # Data rows
1554  133      for row in table[1:]:
1555  134          # Pad row to max_cols if needed
1556  135          row_padded = list(row) + [""] * (max_cols - len(row))
1557  136          markdown_lines.append(
1558  137              "| " + " | ".join(str(cell) if cell else "" for cell in row_padded) + " |"
1559  138          )
1560  139  
1561  140      return "\n".join(markdown_lines)

1564  143  def read_file_content(file_path):
1565  144      """Read file content, handling different file types."""
1566  145      file_ext = os.path.splitext(file_path)[1].lower()
1567  146  
1568  147      if file_ext == ".docx":
1569  148          return extract_docx_text(file_path)
1570  149      elif file_ext == ".pdf":
1571  150          return extract_pdf_text(file_path)
1572  151      else:
1573  152          # Default: read as text
1574  153          # Try UTF-8 first, then raise UnicodeDecodeError if it fails
1575  154          # This preserves the original behavior for binary files
1576  155          with open(file_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
1577  156              return f.read()

1581  160      if cxml:
1582  161          print_as_xml(writer, path, content, line_numbers)
1583  162      elif markdown:
1584  163          print_as_markdown(writer, path, content, line_numbers)
1585  164      else:
1586  165          print_default(writer, path, content, line_numbers)
1587  166  
1588  167  
1589  168  def print_default(writer, path, content, line_numbers):
1590  169      writer(path)
1591  170      writer("---")
1592  171      if line_numbers:
1593  172          content = add_line_numbers(content)
1594  173      writer(content)
1595  174      writer("")
1596  175      writer("---")

1599  178  def print_as_xml(writer, path, content, line_numbers):
1600  179      global global_index
1601  180      writer(f'<document index="{global_index}">')
1602  181      writer(f"<source>{path}</source>")
1603  182      writer("<document_content>")
1604  183      if line_numbers:
1605  184          content = add_line_numbers(content)
1606  185      writer(content)
1607  186      writer("</document_content>")
1608  187      writer("</document>")
1609  188      global_index += 1

1612  191  def print_as_markdown(writer, path, content, line_numbers):
1613  192      lang = EXT_TO_LANG.get(path.split(".")[-1], "")
1614  193      # Figure out how many backticks to use
1615  194      backticks = "```"
1616  195      while backticks in content:
1617  196          backticks += "`"
1618  197      writer(path)
1619  198      writer(f"{backticks}{lang}")
1620  199      if line_numbers:
1621  200          content = add_line_numbers(content)
1622  201      writer(content)
1623  202      writer(f"{backticks}")

1626  205  def process_path(
1627  206      path,
1628  207      extensions,
1629  208      include_hidden,
1630  209      ignore_files_only,
1631  210      ignore_gitignore,
1632  211      gitignore_rules,
1633  212      ignore_patterns,
1634  213      writer,
1635  214      claude_xml,
1636  215      markdown,
1637  216      line_numbers=False,
1638  217  ):
1639  218      if os.path.isfile(path):
1640  219          try:
1641  220              content = read_file_content(path)
1642  221              print_path(writer, path, content, claude_xml, markdown, line_numbers)
1643  222          except UnicodeDecodeError:
1644  223              warning_message = f"Warning: Skipping file {path} due to UnicodeDecodeError"
1645  224              click.echo(click.style(warning_message, fg="red"), err=True)
1646  225          except Exception as e:
1647  226              warning_message = f"Warning: Skipping file {path} due to error: {str(e)}"
1648  227              click.echo(click.style(warning_message, fg="red"), err=True)
1649  228      elif os.path.isdir(path):
1650  229          for root, dirs, files in os.walk(path):
1651  230              if not include_hidden:
1652  231                  dirs[:] = [d for d in dirs if not d.startswith(".")]
1653  232                  files = [f for f in files if not f.startswith(".")]
1654  233  
1655  234              if not ignore_gitignore:
1656  235                  gitignore_rules.extend(read_gitignore(root))
1657  236                  dirs[:] = [
1658  237                      d
1659  238                      for d in dirs
1660  239                      if not should_ignore(os.path.join(root, d), gitignore_rules)
1661  240                  ]
1662  241                  files = [
1663  242                      f
1664  243                      for f in files
1665  244                      if not should_ignore(os.path.join(root, f), gitignore_rules)
1666  245                  ]
1667  246  
1668  247              if ignore_patterns:
1669  248                  if not ignore_files_only:
1670  249                      dirs[:] = [
1671  250                          d
1672  251                          for d in dirs
1673  252                          if not any(fnmatch(d, pattern) for pattern in ignore_patterns)
1674  253                      ]
1675  254                  files = [
1676  255                      f
1677  256                      for f in files
1678  257                      if not any(fnmatch(f, pattern) for pattern in ignore_patterns)
1679  258                  ]
1680  259  
1681  260              if extensions:
1682  261                  files = [f for f in files if f.endswith(extensions)]
1683  262  
1684  263              for file in sorted(files):
1685  264                  file_path = os.path.join(root, file)
1686  265                  try:
1687  266                      content = read_file_content(file_path)
1688  267                      print_path(
1689  268                          writer,
1690  269                          file_path,
1691  270                          content,
1692  271                          claude_xml,
1693  272                          markdown,
1694  273                          line_numbers,
1695  274                      )
1696  275                  except UnicodeDecodeError:
1697  276                      warning_message = (
1698  277                          f"Warning: Skipping file {file_path} due to UnicodeDecodeError"
1699  278                      )
1700  279                      click.echo(click.style(warning_message, fg="red"), err=True)
1701  280                  except Exception as e:
1702  281                      warning_message = (
1703  282                          f"Warning: Skipping file {file_path} due to error: {str(e)}"
1704  283                      )
1705  284                      click.echo(click.style(warning_message, fg="red"), err=True)

1707  286  
1708  287  def read_paths_from_stdin(use_null_separator):
1709  288      if sys.stdin.isatty():
1710  289          # No ready input from stdin, don't block for input
1711  290          return []
1712  291  
1713  292      stdin_content = sys.stdin.read()
1714  293      if use_null_separator:
1715  294          paths = stdin_content.split("\0")
1716  295      else:
1717  296          paths = stdin_content.split()  # split on whitespace
1718  297      return [p for p in paths if p]
1719  298  
1720  299  
1721  300  @click.command()
1722  301  @click.argument("paths", nargs=-1, type=click.Path(exists=True))
1723  302  @click.option("extensions", "-e", "--extension", multiple=True)
1724  303  @click.option(
1725  304      "--include-hidden",
1726  305      is_flag=True,
1727  306      help="Include files and folders starting with .",
1728  307  )
1729  308  @click.option(
1730  309      "--ignore-files-only",
1731  310      is_flag=True,
1732  311      help="--ignore option only ignores files",
1733  312  )
1734  313  @click.option(
1735  314      "--ignore-gitignore",
1736  315      is_flag=True,
1737  316      help="Ignore .gitignore files and include all files",
1738  317  )
1739  318  @click.option(
1740  319      "ignore_patterns",
1741  320      "--ignore",
1742  321      multiple=True,
1743  322      default=[],
1744  323      help="List of patterns to ignore",
1745  324  )
1746  325  @click.option(
1747  326      "output_file",
1748  327      "-o",
1749  328      "--output",
1750  329      type=click.Path(writable=True),
1751  330      help="Output to a file instead of stdout",
1752  331  )
1753  332  @click.option(
1754  333      "claude_xml",
1755  334      "-c",
1756  335      "--cxml",
1757  336      is_flag=True,
1758  337      help="Output in XML-ish format suitable for Claude's long context window.",
1759  338  )
1760  339  @click.option(
1761  340      "markdown",
1762  341      "-m",
1763  342      "--markdown",
1764  343      is_flag=True,
1765  344      help="Output Markdown with fenced code blocks",
1766  345  )
1767  346  @click.option(
1768  347      "line_numbers",
1769  348      "-n",
1770  349      "--line-numbers",
1771  350      is_flag=True,
1772  351      help="Add line numbers to the output",
1773  352  )
1774  353  @click.option(
1775  354      "--null",
1776  355      "-0",
1777  356      is_flag=True,
1778  357      help="Use NUL character as separator when reading from stdin",
1779  358  )
1780  359  @click.version_option()
1781  360  def cli(
1782  361      paths,
1783  362      extensions,
1784  363      include_hidden,
1785  364      ignore_files_only,
1786  365      ignore_gitignore,
1787  366      ignore_patterns,
1788  367      output_file,
1789  368      claude_xml,
1790  369      markdown,
1791  370      line_numbers,
1792  371      null,
1793  372  ):
1794  373      """
1795  374      Takes one or more paths to files or directories and outputs every file,
1796  375      recursively, each one preceded with its filename like this:
1797  376  
1798  377      \b
1799  378          path/to/file.py
1800  379          ----
1801  380          Contents of file.py goes here
1802  381          ---
1803  382          path/to/file2.py
1804  383          ---
1805  384          ...
1806  385  
1807  386      If the `--cxml` flag is provided, the output will be structured as follows:
1808  387  
1809  388      \b
1810  389          <documents>
1811  390          <document path="path/to/file1.txt">
1812  391          Contents of file1.txt
1813  392          </document>
1814  393          <document path="path/to/file2.txt">
1815  394          Contents of file2.txt
1816  395          </document>
1817  396          ...
1818  397          </documents>
1819  398  
1820  399      If the `--markdown` flag is provided, the output will be structured as follows:
1821  400  
1822  401      \b
1823  402          path/to/file1.py
1824  403          ```python
1825  404          Contents of file1.py
1826  405          ```
1827  406      """
1828  407      # Reset global_index for pytest
1829  408      global global_index
1830  409      global_index = 1
1831  410  
1832  411      # Read paths from stdin if available
1833  412      stdin_paths = read_paths_from_stdin(use_null_separator=null)
1834  413  
1835  414      # Combine paths from arguments and stdin
1836  415      paths = [*paths, *stdin_paths]
1837  416  
1838  417      gitignore_rules = []
1839  418      writer = click.echo
1840  419      fp = None
1841  420      if output_file:
1842  421          fp = open(output_file, "w", encoding="utf-8")
1843  422          writer = lambda s: print(s, file=fp)
1844  423      for path in paths:
1845  424          if not os.path.exists(path):
1846  425              raise click.BadArgumentUsage(f"Path does not exist: {path}")
1847  426          if not ignore_gitignore:
1848  427              gitignore_rules.extend(read_gitignore(os.path.dirname(path)))
1849  428          if claude_xml and path == paths[0]:
1850  429              writer("<documents>")
1851  430          process_path(
1852  431              path,
1853  432              extensions,
1854  433              include_hidden,
1855  434              ignore_files_only,
1856  435              ignore_gitignore,
1857  436              gitignore_rules,
1858  437              ignore_patterns,
1859  438              writer,
1860  439              claude_xml,
1861  440              markdown,
1862  441              line_numbers,
1863  442          )
1864  443      if claude_xml:
1865  444          writer("</documents>")
1866  445      if fp:
1867  446          fp.close()

2403     3   1  # Repository Guidelines
2404     4   2  
2405     5   3  ## Project Structure & Modules
2406     6   4  - Core package lives in `files_to_prompt/`: `cli.py` exposes the Click-based CLI, `__main__.py` enables `python -m files_to_prompt`, and `__init__.py` holds package metadata.
2407     7   5  - Tests sit in `tests/test_files_to_prompt.py`; keep new tests in this suite to mirror CLI behaviors.
2408     8   6  - Tooling and metadata are defined in `pyproject.toml`. Runtime dependency footprint is minimal (`click` only); avoid introducing new ones without discussion.
2409     9   7  
2410    10   8  ## Setup, Build, and Development Commands
2411    11   9  - Create an isolated environment: `python -m venv venv && source venv/bin/activate`.
2412    12  10  - Install dependencies for local work: `pip install -e '.[test]'`.
2413    13  11  - Run the CLI during development without installing globally: `python -m files_to_prompt path/to/dir -m` or `python -m files_to_prompt --help`.
2414    14  12  - Package metadata is driven by `pyproject.toml`; bump versions there when preparing releases.
2415    15  13  
2416    16  14  ## Coding Style & Naming Conventions
2417    17  15  - Follow standard Python 3.8+ conventions: 4-space indentation, snake_case for functions/variables, and meaningful, lowercase CLI option names.
2418    18  16  - Keep functions small and reuse existing helpers (e.g., `process_path`, `print_as_markdown`) rather than adding branching in `cli()`.
2419    19  17  - Prefer stdlib solutions; avoid new dependencies unless they deliver clear value.
2420    20  18  - Match current import style (stdlib first, blank line, third-party).
2421    21  19  
2422    22  20  ## Testing Guidelines
2423    23  21  - Primary test runner: `pytest`.
2424    24  22  - Add or extend cases in `tests/test_files_to_prompt.py` when modifying CLI flags, output formats, or ignore rules.
2425    25  23  - Include edge cases (hidden files, ignored paths, mixed encodings) and assert on concrete output strings, since the tool is output-centric.
2426    26  24  - Run `pytest` before opening a PR; aim for coverage of new code paths rather than global percentage targets.
2427    27  25  
2428    28  26  ## Commit & Pull Request Guidelines
2429    29  27  - Use concise, imperative commit subjects (e.g., `Add markdown line-number option`, `Refine ignore patterns`). One logical change per commit where possible.
2430    30  28  - PRs should summarize intent, list main changes, and note testing performed (`pytest`). Link issues when they exist and include sample CLI output for user-facing changes.
2431    31  29  - Keep diffs small and readable; prefer refactors in separate PRs from feature additions.
2432    32  30  
2433    33  31  ## Security & Configuration Tips
2434    34  32  - The CLI reads files recursively; respect repository `.gitignore` handling and default hidden-file exclusion to avoid leaking secrets in prompts.
2435    35  33  - When adding new options that affect file selection or output destinations, validate user inputs and maintain safe defaults (no overwriting unless requested).
2436    36  ```
2437    37  ./README.md
2438    38  ``````
2439    39    1  # files-to-prompt
2440    40    2  
2441    41    3  [![PyPI](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/files-to-prompt.svg)](https://pypi.org/project/files-to-prompt/)
2442    42    4  [![Changelog](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/simonw/files-to-prompt?include_prereleases&label=changelog)](https://github.com/simonw/files-to-prompt/releases)
2443    43    5  [![Tests](https://github.com/simonw/files-to-prompt/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/simonw/files-to-prompt/actions/workflows/test.yml)
2444    44    6  [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache%202.0-blue.svg)](https://github.com/simonw/files-to-prompt/blob/master/LICENSE)
2445    45    7  
2446    46    8  Concatenate a directory full of files into a single prompt for use with LLMs
2447    47    9  
2448    48   10  For background on this project see [Building files-to-prompt entirely using Claude 3 Opus](https://simonwillison.net/2024/Apr/8/files-to-prompt/).
2449    49   11  
2450    50   12  ## Installation
2451    51   13  
2452    52   14  Install this tool using `pip`:
2453    53   15  
2454    54   16  ```bash
2455    55   17  pip install files-to-prompt
2456    56   18  ```
2457    57   19  
2458    58   20  ## Usage
2459    59   21  
2460    60   22  To use `files-to-prompt`, provide the path to one or more files or directories you want to process:
2461    61   23  
2462    62   24  ```bash
2463    63   25  files-to-prompt path/to/file_or_directory [path/to/another/file_or_directory ...]
2464    64   26  ```
2465    65   27  
2466    66   28  This will output the contents of every file, with each file preceded by its relative path and separated by `---`.
2467    67   29  
2468    68   30  ### Options
2469    69   31  
2470    70   32  - `-e/--extension <extension>`: Only include files with the specified extension. Can be used multiple times.
2471    71   33  
2472    72   34    ```bash
2473    73   35    files-to-prompt path/to/directory -e txt -e md
2474    74   36    ```
2475    75   37  
2476    76   38  - `--include-hidden`: Include files and folders starting with `.` (hidden files and directories).
2477    77   39  
2478    78   40    ```bash
2479    79   41    files-to-prompt path/to/directory --include-hidden
2480    80   42    ```
2481    81   43  
2482    82   44  - `--ignore <pattern>`: Specify one or more patterns to ignore. Can be used multiple times. Patterns may match file names and directory names, unless you also specify `--ignore-files-only`. Pattern syntax uses [fnmatch](https://docs.python.org/3/library/fnmatch.html), which supports `*`, `?`, `[anychar]`, `[!notchars]` and `[?]` for special character literals.
2483    83   45    ```bash
2484    84   46    files-to-prompt path/to/directory --ignore "*.log" --ignore "temp*"
2485    85   47    ```
2486    86   48  
2487    87   49  - `--ignore-files-only`: Include directory paths which would otherwise be ignored by an `--ignore` pattern.
2488    88   50  
2489    89   51    ```bash
2490    90   52    files-to-prompt path/to/directory --ignore-files-only --ignore "*dir*"
2491    91   53    ```
2492    92   54  
2493    93   55  - `--ignore-gitignore`: Ignore `.gitignore` files and include all files.
2494    94   56  
2495    95   57    ```bash
2496    96   58    files-to-prompt path/to/directory --ignore-gitignore
2497    97   59    ```
2498    98   60  
2499    99   61  - `-c/--cxml`: Output in Claude XML format.
2500   100   62  
2501   101   63    ```bash
2502   102   64    files-to-prompt path/to/directory --cxml
2503   103   65    ```
2504   104   66  
2505   105   67  - `-m/--markdown`: Output as Markdown with fenced code blocks.
2506   106   68  
2507   107   69    ```bash
2508   108   70    files-to-prompt path/to/directory --markdown
2509   109   71    ```
2510   110   72  
2511   111   73  - `-o/--output <file>`: Write the output to a file instead of printing it to the console.
2512   112   74  
2513   113   75    ```bash
2514   114   76    files-to-prompt path/to/directory -o output.txt
2515   115   77    ```
2516   116   78  
2517   117   79  - `-n/--line-numbers`: Include line numbers in the output.
2518   118   80  
2519   119   81    ```bash
2520   120   82    files-to-prompt path/to/directory -n
2521   121   83    ```
2522   122   84    Example output:
2523   123   85    ```
2524   124   86    files_to_prompt/cli.py
2525   125   87    ---
2526   126   88      1  import os
2527   127   89      2  from fnmatch import fnmatch
2528   128   90      3
2529   129   91      4  import click
2530   130   92      ...
2531   131   93    ```
2532   132   94  
2533   133   95  - `-0/--null`: Use NUL character as separator when reading paths from stdin. Useful when filenames may contain spaces.
2534   134   96  
2535   135   97    ```bash
2536   136   98    find . -name "*.py" -print0 | files-to-prompt --null
2537   137   99    ```
2538   138  100  
2539   139  101  ### Example
2540   140  102  
2541   141  103  Suppose you have a directory structure like this:
2542   142  104  
2543   143  105  ```
2544   144  106  my_directory/
2545   145  107  ├── file1.txt
2546   146  108  ├── file2.txt
2547   147  109  ├── .hidden_file.txt
2548   148  110  ├── temp.log
2549   149  111  └── subdirectory/
2550   150  112      └── file3.txt
2551   151  113  ```
2552   152  114  
2553   153  115  Running `files-to-prompt my_directory` will output:
2554   154  116  
2555   155  117  ```
2556   156  118  my_directory/file1.txt
2557   157  119  ---
2558   158  120  Contents of file1.txt
2559   159  121  ---
2560   160  122  my_directory/file2.txt
2561   161  123  ---
2562   162  124  Contents of file2.txt
2563   163  125  ---
2564   164  126  my_directory/subdirectory/file3.txt
2565   165  127  ---
2566   166  128  Contents of file3.txt
2567   167  129  ---
2568   168  130  ```
2569   169  131  
2570   170  132  If you run `files-to-prompt my_directory --include-hidden`, the output will also include `.hidden_file.txt`:
2571   171  133  
2572   172  134  ```
2573   173  135  my_directory/.hidden_file.txt
2574   174  136  ---
2575   175  137  Contents of .hidden_file.txt
2576   176  138  ---
2577   177  139  ...
2578   178  140  ```
2579   179  141  
2580   180  142  If you run `files-to-prompt my_directory --ignore "*.log"`, the output will exclude `temp.log`:
2581   181  143  
2582   182  144  ```
2583   183  145  my_directory/file1.txt
2584   184  146  ---
2585   185  147  Contents of file1.txt
2586   186  148  ---
2587   187  149  my_directory/file2.txt
2588   188  150  ---
2589   189  151  Contents of file2.txt
2590   190  152  ---
2591   191  153  my_directory/subdirectory/file3.txt
2592   192  154  ---
2593   193  155  Contents of file3.txt
2594   194  156  ---
2595   195  157  ```
2596   196  158  
2597   197  159  If you run `files-to-prompt my_directory --ignore "sub*"`, the output will exclude all files in `subdirectory/` (unless you also specify `--ignore-files-only`):
2598   198  160  
2599   199  161  ```
2600   200  162  my_directory/file1.txt
2601   201  163  ---
2602   202  164  Contents of file1.txt
2603   203  165  ---
2604   204  166  my_directory/file2.txt
2605   205  167  ---
2606   206  168  Contents of file2.txt
2607   207  169  ---
2608   208  170  ```
2609   209  171  
2610   210  172  ### Reading from stdin
2611   211  173  
2612   212  174  The tool can also read paths from standard input. This can be used to pipe in the output of another command:
2613   213  175  
2614   214  176  ```bash
2615   215  177  # Find files modified in the last day
2616   216  178  find . -mtime -1 | files-to-prompt
2617   217  179  ```
2618   218  180  
2619   219  181  When using the `--null` (or `-0`) option, paths are expected to be NUL-separated (useful when dealing with filenames containing spaces):
2620   220  182  
2621   221  183  ```bash
2622   222  184  find . -name "*.txt" -print0 | files-to-prompt --null
2623   223  185  ```
2624   224  186  
2625   225  187  You can mix and match paths from command line arguments and stdin:
2626   226  188  
2627   227  189  ```bash
2628   228  190  # Include files modified in the last day, and also include README.md
2629   229  191  find . -mtime -1 | files-to-prompt README.md
2630   230  192  ```
2631   231  193  
2632   232  194  ### Claude XML Output
2633   233  195  
2634   234  196  Anthropic has provided [specific guidelines](https://docs.anthropic.com/claude/docs/long-context-window-tips) for optimally structuring prompts to take advantage of Claude's extended context window.
2635   235  197  
2636   236  198  To structure the output in this way, use the optional `--cxml` flag, which will produce output like this:
2637   237  199  
2638   238  200  ```xml
2639   239  201  <documents>
2640   240  202  <document index="1">
2641   241  203  <source>my_directory/file1.txt</source>
2642   242  204  <document_content>
2643   243  205  Contents of file1.txt
2644   244  206  </document_content>
2645   245  207  </document>
2646   246  208  <document index="2">
2647   247  209  <source>my_directory/file2.txt</source>
2648   248  210  <document_content>
2649   249  211  Contents of file2.txt
2650   250  212  </document_content>
2651   251  213  </document>
2652   252  214  </documents>
2653   253  215  ```
2654   254  216  
2655   255  217  ## --markdown fenced code block output
2656   256  218  
2657   257  219  The `--markdown` option will output the files as fenced code blocks, which can be useful for pasting into Markdown documents.
2658   258  220  
2659   259  221  ```bash
2660   260  222  files-to-prompt path/to/directory --markdown
2661   261  223  ```
2662   262  224  The language tag will be guessed based on the filename.
2663   263  225  
2664   264  226  If the code itself contains triple backticks the wrapper around it will use one additional backtick.
2665   265  227  
2666   266  228  Example output:
2667   267  229  `````
2668   268  230  myfile.py
2669   269  231  ```python
2670   270  232  def my_function():
2671   271  233      return "Hello, world!"
2672   272  234  ```
2673   273  235  other.js
2674   274  236  ```javascript
2675   275  237  function myFunction() {
2676   276  238      return "Hello, world!";
2677   277  239  }
2678   278  240  ```
2679   279  241  file_with_triple_backticks.md
2680   280  242  ````markdown
2681   281  243  This file has its own
2682   282  244  ```
2683   283  245  fenced code blocks
2684   284  246  ```
2685   285  247  Inside it.
2686   286  248  ````
2687   287  249  `````
2688   288  250  
2689   289  251  ## Development
2690   290  252  
2691   291  253  To contribute to this tool, first checkout the code. Then create a new virtual environment:
2692   292  254  
2693   293  255  ```bash
2694   294  256  cd files-to-prompt
2695   295  257  python -m venv venv
2696   296  258  source venv/bin/activate
2697   297  259  ```
2698   298  260  
2699   299  261  Now install the dependencies and test dependencies:
2700   300  262  
2701   301  263  ```bash
2702   302  264  pip install -e '.[test]'
2703   303  265  ```
2704   304  266  
2705   305  267  To run the tests:
2706   306  268  
2707   307  269  ```bash
2708   308  270  pytest
2709   309  271  ```

3941  1541  120  def format_table_as_markdown(table):
3942  1542  121      """Format a table (list of lists) as markdown table."""
3943  1543  122      if not table or not table[0]:
3944  1544  123          return ""
3945  1545  124  
3946  1546  125      # Find the maximum number of columns across all rows
3947  1547  126      max_cols = max(len(row) for row in table if row)
3948  1548  127  
3949  1549  128      markdown_lines = []
3950  1550  129      # Header row
3951  1551  130      header = table[0]
3952  1552  131      # Pad header to max_cols if needed
3953  1553  132      header_padded = list(header) + [""] * (max_cols - len(header))
3954  1554  133      markdown_lines.append("| " + " | ".join(str(cell) if cell else "" for cell in header_padded) + " |")
3955  1555  134      markdown_lines.append("| " + " | ".join("---" for _ in range(max_cols)) + " |")
3956  1556  135  
3957  1557  136      # Data rows
3958  1558  137      for row in table[1:]:
3959  1559  138          # Pad row to max_cols if needed
3960  1560  139          row_padded = list(row) + [""] * (max_cols - len(row))
3961  1561  140          markdown_lines.append("| " + " | ".join(str(cell) if cell else "" for cell in row_padded) + " |")
3962  1562  141  
3963  1563  142      return "\n".join(markdown_lines)

4023  1623  202      lang = EXT_TO_LANG.get(path.split(".")[-1], "")

4191  1791  370  def cli(
4192  1792  371      paths,
4193  1793  372      extensions,
4194  1794  373      include_hidden,
4195  1795  374      ignore_files_only,
4196  1796  375      ignore_gitignore,
4197  1797  376      ignore_patterns,
4198  1798  377      output_file,
4199  1799  378      claude_xml,
4200  1800  379      markdown,

4202  1802  381      null,
4203  1803  382  ):
4204  1804  383      """
4205  1805  384      Takes one or more paths to files or directories and outputs every file,
4206  1806  385      recursively, each one preceded with its filename like this:
4207  1807  386  
4208  1808  387      \b
4209  1809  388          path/to/file.py
4210  1810  389          ----
4211  1811  390          Contents of file.py goes here
4212  1812  391          ---
4213  1813  392          path/to/file2.py
4214  1814  393          ---
4215  1815  394          ...
4216  1816  395  
4217  1817  396      If the `--cxml` flag is provided, the output will be structured as follows:
4218  1818  397  
4219  1819  398      \b
4220  1820  399          <documents>
4221  1821  400          <document path="path/to/file1.txt">
4222  1822  401          Contents of file1.txt
4223  1823  402          </document>
4224  1824  403          <document path="path/to/file2.txt">
4225  1825  404          Contents of file2.txt
4226  1826  405          </document>
4227  1827  406          ...
4228  1828  407          </documents>
4229  1829  408  
4230  1830  409      If the `--markdown` flag is provided, the output will be structured as follows:
4231  1831  410  
4232  1832  411      \b
4233  1833  412          path/to/file1.py
4234  1834  413          ```python
4235  1835  414          Contents of file1.py
4236  1836  415          ```
4237  1837  416      """
4238  1838  417      # Reset global_index for pytest
4239  1839  418      global global_index
4240  1840  419      global_index = 1
4241  1841  420  
4242  1842  421      # Read paths from stdin if available
4243  1843  422      stdin_paths = read_paths_from_stdin(use_null_separator=null)
4244  1844  423  
4245  1845  424      # Combine paths from arguments and stdin
4246  1846  425      paths = [*paths, *stdin_paths]
4247  1847  426  
4248  1848  427      gitignore_rules = []
4249  1849  428      writer = click.echo
4250  1850  429      fp = None
4251  1851  430      if output_file:
4252  1852  431          fp = open(output_file, "w", encoding="utf-8")
4253  1853  432          writer = lambda s: print(s, file=fp)
4254  1854  433      for path in paths:
4255  1855  434          if not os.path.exists(path):
4256  1856  435              raise click.BadArgumentUsage(f"Path does not exist: {path}")

4262  1862  441              path,
4263  1863  442              extensions,
4264  1864  443              include_hidden,

4267  1867  446              gitignore_rules,
4268  1868  447              ignore_patterns,

5617  3217    5  Gemini 3 is our most intelligent model family to date, built on a
5618  3218    6  foundation of state-of-the-art reasoning. It is designed to bring any
5619  3219    7  idea to life by mastering agentic workflows, autonomous coding, and
5620  3220    8  complex multimodal tasks. This guide covers key features of the Gemini 3
5621  3221    9  model family and how to get the most out of it.
5622  3222   10  
5623  3223   11  High/Dynamic Thinking Low Thinking
5624  3224   12  
5625  3225   13  Gemini 3 Pro uses dynamic thinking by default to reason through prompts.
5626  3226   14  For faster, lower-latency responses when complex reasoning isn\'t
5627  3227   15  required, you can constrain the model\'s thinking level to low.
5628  3228   16
