5687  3287   75  New API features in Gemini 3
5688  3288   76  
5689  3289   77  Gemini 3 introduces new parameters designed to give developers more
5690  3290   78  control over latency, cost, and multimodal fidelity.
5691  3291   79  
5692  3292   80  Thinking level
5693  3293   81  
5694  3294   82  The thinking_level parameter controls the **maximum** depth of the
5695  3295   83  model\'s internal reasoning process before it produces a response.
5696  3296   84  Gemini 3 treats these levels as relative allowances for thinking rather
5697  3297   85  than strict token guarantees. If thinking_level is not specified, Gemini
5698  3298   86  3 Pro will default to high.
5699  3299   87  
5700  3300   88  - low: Minimizes latency and cost. Best for simple instruction
5701  3301   89    following, chat, or high-throughput applications
5702  3302   90  
5703  3303   91  - medium: (Coming soon), not supported at launch
5704  3304   92  
5705  3305   93  - high (Default): Maximizes reasoning depth. The model may take
5706  3306   94    significantly longer to reach a first token, but the output will be
5707  3307   95    more carefully reasoned.
5708  3308   96  
5709  3309   97  **Warning:** You cannot use both **thinking_level** and the
5710  3310   98  legacy **thinking_budget** parameter in the same request. Doing so will
5711  3311   99  return a 400 error.
5712  3312  100  
5713  3313  101  Media resolution
5714  3314  102  
5715  3315  103  Gemini 3 introduces granular control over multimodal vision processing
5716  3316  104  via the media_resolution parameter. Higher resolutions improve the
5717  3317  105  model\'s ability to read fine text or identify small details, but
5718  3318  106  increase token usage and latency. The media_resolution parameter
5719  3319  107  determines the **maximum number of tokens allocated per input image or
5720  3320  108  video frame.**
5721  3321  109  
5722  3322  110  You can now set the resolution
5723  3323  111  to media_resolution_low, media_resolution_medium,
5724  3324  112  or media_resolution_high per individual media part or globally
5725  3325  113  (via generation_config). If unspecified, the model uses optimal defaults
5726  3326  114  based on the media type.
5727  3327  115  
5728  3328  116  **Recommended settings**
5729  3329  117  
5730  3330  118    ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5731  3331  119    Media Type           Recommended Setting                                 Max      Usage Guidance
5732  3332  120                                                                             Tokens   
5733  3333  121    -------------------- --------------------------------------------------- -------- --------------------------------
5734  3334  122    Images               media_resolution_high                               1120     Recommended for most image
5735  3335  123                                                                                      analysis tasks to ensure maximum
5736  3336  124                                                                                      quality.
5737  3337  125  
5738  3338  126    PDFs                 media_resolution_medium                             560      Optimal for document
5739  3339  127                                                                                      understanding; quality typically
5740  3340  128                                                                                      saturates at medium. Increasing
5741  3341  129                                                                                      to high rarely improves OCR
5742  3342  130                                                                                      results for standard documents.
5743  3343  131  
5744  3344  132    Video (General)      media_resolution_low (or media_resolution_medium)   70 (per  Note: For
5745  3345  133                                                                             frame)   video, low and medium settings
5746  3346  134                                                                                      are treated identically (70
5747  3347  135                                                                                      tokens) to optimize context
5748  3348  136                                                                                      usage. This is sufficient for
5749  3349  137                                                                                      most action recognition and
5750  3350  138                                                                                      description tasks.
5751  3351  139  
5752  3352  140    Video (Text-heavy)   media_resolution_high                               280 (per Required only when the use case
5753  3353  141                                                                             frame)   involves reading dense text
5754  3354  142                                                                                      (OCR) or small details within
5755  3355  143                                                                                      video frames.
5756  3356  144    ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5757  3357  145  
5758  3358  146  **Note:** The **media_resolution** parameter maps to different token
5759  3359  147  counts depending on the input type. While images scale linearly
5760  3360  148  (**media_resolution_low**: 280, **media_resolution_medium**:
5761  3361  149  560, **media_resolution_high**: 1120), Video is compressed more
5762  3362  150  aggressively. For Video,
5763  3363  151  both **media_resolution_low** and **media_resolution_medium** are capped
5764  3364  152  at 70 tokens per frame, and **media_resolution_high** is capped at 280
5765  3365  153  tokens. See full
5766  3366  154  details [[here]{.underline}](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/media-resolution#token-counts)
5767  3367  155

5817  3417  205  Temperature
5818  3418  206  
5819  3419  207  For Gemini 3, we strongly recommend keeping the temperature parameter at
5820  3420  208  its default value of 1.0.
5821  3421  209  
5822  3422  210  While previous models often benefited from tuning temperature to control
5823  3423  211  creativity versus determinism, Gemini 3\'s reasoning capabilities are
5824  3424  212  optimized for the default setting. Changing the temperature (setting it
5825  3425  213  below 1.0) may lead to unexpected behavior, such as looping or degraded
5826  3426  214  performance, particularly in complex mathematical or reasoning tasks.
5827  3427  215  
5828  3428  216  Thought signatures
5829  3429  217  
5830  3430  218  Gemini 3 uses [[Thought
5831  3431  219  signatures]{.underline}](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/thought-signatures) to
5832  3432  220  maintain reasoning context across API calls. These signatures are
5833  3433  221  encrypted representations of the model\'s internal thought process. To
5834  3434  222  ensure the model maintains its reasoning capabilities you must return
5835  3435  223  these signatures back to the model in your request exactly as they were
5836  3436  224  received:
5837  3437  225  
5838  3438  226  - **Function Calling (Strict):** The API enforces strict validation on
5839  3439  227    the \"Current Turn\". Missing signatures will result in a 400 error.
5840  3440  228  
5841  3441  229  - **Text/Chat:** Validation is not strictly enforced, but omitting
5842  3442  230    signatures will degrade the model\'s reasoning and answer quality.
5843  3443  231  
5844  3444  232  - **Image generation/editing (Strict)**: The API enforces strict
5845  3445  233    validation on all Model parts including a thoughtSignature. Missing
5846  3446  234    signatures will result in a 400 error.
5847  3447  235  
5848  3448  236  **Success:** If you use the [[official SDKs (Python, Node,
5849  3449  237  Java)]{.underline}](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/function-calling?example=meeting#thinking) and
5850  3450  238  standard chat history, Thought Signatures are handled automatically. You
5851  3451  239  do not need to manually manage these fields.
5852  3452  240  
5853  3453  241  Function calling (strict validation)
5854  3454  242  
5855  3455  243  When Gemini generates a functionCall, it relies on
5856  3456  244  the thoughtSignature to process the tool\'s output correctly in the next
5857  3457  245  turn. The \"Current Turn\" includes all Model (functionCall) and User
5858  3458  246  (functionResponse) steps that occurred since the last
5859  3459  247  standard **User** text message.
5860  3460  248  
5861  3461  249  - **Single Function Call:** The functionCall part contains a signature.
5862  3462  250    You must return it.
5863  3463  251  
5864  3464  252  - **Parallel Function Calls:** Only the first functionCall part in the
5865  3465  253    list will contain the signature. You must return the parts in the
5866  3466  254    exact order received.
5867  3467  255  
5868  3468  256  - **Multi-Step (Sequential):** If the model calls a tool, receives a
5869  3469  257    result, and calls *another* tool (within the same
5870  3470  258    turn), **both** function calls have signatures. You must
5871  3471  259    return **all** accumulated signatures in the history.
5872  3472  260  
5873  3473  261  Text and streaming
5874  3474  262  
5875  3475  263  For standard chat or text generation, the presence of a signature is not
5876  3476  264  guaranteed.
5877  3477  265  
5878  3478  266  - **Non-Streaming**: The final content part of the response may contain
5879  3479  267    a thoughtSignature, though it is not always present. If one is
5880  3480  268    returned, you should send it back to maintain best performance.
5881  3481  269  
5882  3482  270  - **Streaming**: If a signature is generated, it may arrive in a final
5883  3483  271    chunk that contains an empty text part. Ensure your stream parser
5884  3484  272    checks for signatures even if the text field is empty.
5885  3485  273  
5886  3486  274  Image generation and editing
5887  3487  275  
5888  3488  276  For gemini-3-pro-image-preview, thought signatures are critical for
5889  3489  277  conversational editing. When you ask the model to modify an image it
5890  3490  278  relies on the thoughtSignature from the previous turn to understand the
5891  3491  279  composition and logic of the original image.
5892  3492  280  
5893  3493  281  - **Editing:** Signatures are guaranteed on the first part after the
5894  3494  282    thoughts of the response (text or inlineData) and on every
5895  3495  283    subsequent inlineData part. You must return all of these signatures to
5896  3496  284    avoid errors.

5976  3576  364  Image generation
5977  3577  365  
5978  3578  366  Gemini 3 Pro Image lets you generate and edit images from text prompts.
5979  3579  367  It uses reasoning to \"think\" through a prompt and can retrieve
5980  3580  368  real-time data---such as weather forecasts or stock charts---before
5981  3581  369  using [[Google
5982  3582  370  Search]{.underline}](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/google-search) grounding
5983  3583  371  before generating high-fidelity images.
5984  3584  372  
5985  3585  373  **New & improved capabilities:**
5986  3586  374  
5987  3587  375  - **Native 4K & text rendering:** Generate sharp, legible text and
5988  3588  376    diagrams with native upscaling to 2K and 4K resolutions.
5989  3589  377  
5990  3590  378  - **Grounded generation:** Use the google_search tool to verify facts
5991  3591  379    and generate imagery based on real-world information.
5992  3592  380  
5993  3593  381  - **Conversational editing:** Multi-turn image editing by simply asking
5994  3594  382    for changes (e.g., \"Make the background a sunset\"). This workflow
5995  3595  383    relies on **Thought Signatures** to preserve visual context between
5996  3596  384    turns.
5997  3597  385  
5998  3598  386  For complete details on aspect ratios, editing workflows, and
5999  3599  387  configuration options, see the [[Image Generation
6000  3600  388  guide]{.underline}](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/image-generation).

6047  3647  435  Migrating from Gemini 2.5
6048  3648  436  
6049  3649  437  Gemini 3 is our most capable model family to date and offers a stepwise
6050  3650  438  improvement over Gemini 2.5 Pro. When migrating, consider the following:
6051  3651  439  
6052  3652  440  - **Thinking:** If you were previously using complex prompt engineering
6053  3653  441    (like Chain-of-thought) to force Gemini 2.5 to reason, try Gemini 3
6054  3654  442    with thinking_level: \"high\" and simplified prompts.
6055  3655  443  
6056  3656  444  - **Temperature settings:** If your existing code explicitly sets
6057  3657  445    temperature (especially to low values for deterministic outputs), we
6058  3658  446    recommend removing this parameter and using the Gemini 3 default of
6059  3659  447    1.0 to avoid potential looping issues or performance degradation on
6060  3660  448    complex tasks.
6061  3661  449  
6062  3662  450  - **PDF & document understanding:** Default OCR resolution for PDFs has
6063  3663  451    changed. If you relied on specific behavior for dense document
6064  3664  452    parsing, test the new media_resolution_high setting to ensure
6065  3665  453    continued accuracy.
6066  3666  454  
6067  3667  455  - **Token consumption:** Migrating to Gemini 3 Pro defaults
6068  3668  456    may **increase** token usage for PDFs but **decrease** token usage for
6069  3669  457    video. If requests now exceed the context window due to higher default
6070  3670  458    resolutions, we recommend explicitly reducing the media resolution.
6071  3671  459  
6072  3672  460  - **Image segmentation:** Image segmentation capabilities (returning
6073  3673  461    pixel-level masks for objects) are not supported in Gemini 3 Pro. For
6074  3674  462    workloads requiring native image segmentation, we recommend continuing
6075  3675  463    to utilize Gemini 2.5 Flash with thinking turned off or [[Gemini
6076  3676  464    Robotics-ER
6077  3677  465    1.5]{.underline}](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/robotics-overview).
6078  3678  466  
6079  3679  467  OpenAI compatibility
6080  3680  468  
6081  3681  469  For users utilizing the OpenAI compatibility layer, standard parameters
6082  3682  470  are automatically mapped to Gemini equivalents:
6083  3683  471  
6084  3684  472  - reasoning_effort (OAI) maps to thinking_level (Gemini). Note
6085  3685  473    that reasoning_effort medium maps to thinking_level high.
6086  3686  474  
6087  3687  475  Prompting best practices
6088  3688  476  
6089  3689  477  Gemini 3 is a reasoning model, which changes how you should prompt.
6090  3690  478  
6091  3691  479  - **Precise instructions:** Be concise in your input prompts. Gemini 3
6092  3692  480    responds best to direct, clear instructions. It may over-analyze
6093  3693  481    verbose or overly complex prompt engineering techniques used for older
6094  3694  482    models.
6095  3695  483  
6096  3696  484  - **Output verbosity:** By default, Gemini 3 is less verbose and prefers
6097  3697  485    providing direct, efficient answers. If your use case requires a more
6098  3698  486    conversational or \"chatty\" persona, you must explicitly steer the
6099  3699  487    model in the prompt (e.g., \"Explain this as a friendly, talkative
6100  3700  488    assistant\").
6101  3701  489  
6102  3702  490  - **Context management:** When working with large datasets (e.g., entire
6103  3703  491    books, codebases, or long videos), place your specific instructions or
6104  3704  492    questions at the end of the prompt, after the data context. Anchor the
6105  3705  493    model\'s reasoning to the provided data by starting your question with
6106  3706  494    a phrase like, \"Based on the information above\...\".
6107  3707  495  
6108  3708  496  Learn more about prompt design strategies in the [[prompt engineering
6109  3709  497  guide]{.underline}](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/prompting-strategies).

6967    1  Gemini 3 Developer Guide
6968    2  
6969    3  content_copy
6970    4  
6971    5  Gemini 3 is our most intelligent model family to date, built on a
6972    6  foundation of state-of-the-art reasoning. It is designed to bring any
6973    7  idea to life by mastering agentic workflows, autonomous coding, and
6974    8  complex multimodal tasks. This guide covers key features of the Gemini 3
6975    9  model family and how to get the most out of it.
6976   10  
6977   11  High/Dynamic Thinking Low Thinking
6978   12  
6979   13  Gemini 3 Pro uses dynamic thinking by default to reason through prompts.
6980   14  For faster, lower-latency responses when complex reasoning isn\'t
6981   15  required, you can constrain the model\'s thinking level to low.
6982   16  
6983   17  [[Python](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/gemini-3?thinking=high#python)[JavaScript](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/gemini-3?thinking=high#javascript)[REST](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/gemini-3?thinking=high#rest)]{.underline}

7040   74  
7041   75  New API features in Gemini 3
7042   76  
7043   77  Gemini 3 introduces new parameters designed to give developers more
7044   78  control over latency, cost, and multimodal fidelity.
7045   79  
7046   80  Thinking level
7047   81  
7048   82  The thinking_level parameter controls the **maximum** depth of the
7049   83  model\'s internal reasoning process before it produces a response.
7050   84  Gemini 3 treats these levels as relative allowances for thinking rather
7051   85  than strict token guarantees. If thinking_level is not specified, Gemini
7052   86  3 Pro will default to high.
7053   87  
7054   88  - low: Minimizes latency and cost. Best for simple instruction
7055   89    following, chat, or high-throughput applications
7056   90  
7057   91  - medium: (Coming soon), not supported at launch
7058   92  
7059   93  - high (Default): Maximizes reasoning depth. The model may take
7060   94    significantly longer to reach a first token, but the output will be
7061   95    more carefully reasoned.
7062   96  
7063   97  **Warning:** You cannot use both **thinking_level** and the
7064   98  legacy **thinking_budget** parameter in the same request. Doing so will
7065   99  return a 400 error.
7066  100  
7067  101  Media resolution
7068  102  
7069  103  Gemini 3 introduces granular control over multimodal vision processing
7070  104  via the media_resolution parameter. Higher resolutions improve the
7071  105  model\'s ability to read fine text or identify small details, but
7072  106  increase token usage and latency. The media_resolution parameter
7073  107  determines the **maximum number of tokens allocated per input image or
7074  108  video frame.**
7075  109  
7076  110  You can now set the resolution
7077  111  to media_resolution_low, media_resolution_medium,
7078  112  or media_resolution_high per individual media part or globally
7079  113  (via generation_config). If unspecified, the model uses optimal defaults
7080  114  based on the media type.
7081  115  
7082  116  **Recommended settings**
7083  117  
7084  118    ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7085  119    Media Type           Recommended Setting                                 Max      Usage Guidance
7086  120                                                                             Tokens   
7087  121    -------------------- --------------------------------------------------- -------- --------------------------------
7088  122    Images               media_resolution_high                               1120     Recommended for most image
7089  123                                                                                      analysis tasks to ensure maximum
7090  124                                                                                      quality.
7091  125  
7092  126    PDFs                 media_resolution_medium                             560      Optimal for document
7093  127                                                                                      understanding; quality typically
7094  128                                                                                      saturates at medium. Increasing
7095  129                                                                                      to high rarely improves OCR
7096  130                                                                                      results for standard documents.
7097  131  
7098  132    Video (General)      media_resolution_low (or media_resolution_medium)   70 (per  Note: For
7099  133                                                                             frame)   video, low and medium settings
7100  134                                                                                      are treated identically (70
7101  135                                                                                      tokens) to optimize context
7102  136                                                                                      usage. This is sufficient for
7103  137                                                                                      most action recognition and
7104  138                                                                                      description tasks.
7105  139  
7106  140    Video (Text-heavy)   media_resolution_high                               280 (per Required only when the use case
7107  141                                                                             frame)   involves reading dense text
7108  142                                                                                      (OCR) or small details within
7109  143                                                                                      video frames.
7110  144    ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7111  145  
7112  146  **Note:** The **media_resolution** parameter maps to different token
7113  147  counts depending on the input type. While images scale linearly
7114  148  (**media_resolution_low**: 280, **media_resolution_medium**:
7115  149  560, **media_resolution_high**: 1120), Video is compressed more
7116  150  aggressively. For Video,
7117  151  both **media_resolution_low** and **media_resolution_medium** are capped
7118  152  at 70 tokens per frame, and **media_resolution_high** is capped at 280
7119  153  tokens. See full
7120  154  details [[here]{.underline}](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/media-resolution#token-counts)
7121  155  
7122  156  [[Python](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/gemini-3?thinking=high#python)[JavaScript](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/gemini-3?thinking=high#javascript)[REST](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/gemini-3?thinking=high#rest)]{.underline}

7171  205  Temperature
7172  206  
7173  207  For Gemini 3, we strongly recommend keeping the temperature parameter at
7174  208  its default value of 1.0.
7175  209  
7176  210  While previous models often benefited from tuning temperature to control
7177  211  creativity versus determinism, Gemini 3\'s reasoning capabilities are
7178  212  optimized for the default setting. Changing the temperature (setting it
7179  213  below 1.0) may lead to unexpected behavior, such as looping or degraded
7180  214  performance, particularly in complex mathematical or reasoning tasks.
7181  215  
7182  216  Thought signatures
7183  217  
7184  218  Gemini 3 uses [[Thought
7185  219  signatures]{.underline}](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/thought-signatures) to
7186  220  maintain reasoning context across API calls. These signatures are
7187  221  encrypted representations of the model\'s internal thought process. To
7188  222  ensure the model maintains its reasoning capabilities you must return
7189  223  these signatures back to the model in your request exactly as they were
7190  224  received:
7191  225  
7192  226  - **Function Calling (Strict):** The API enforces strict validation on
7193  227    the \"Current Turn\". Missing signatures will result in a 400 error.
7194  228  
7195  229  - **Text/Chat:** Validation is not strictly enforced, but omitting
7196  230    signatures will degrade the model\'s reasoning and answer quality.
7197  231  
7198  232  - **Image generation/editing (Strict)**: The API enforces strict
7199  233    validation on all Model parts including a thoughtSignature. Missing
7200  234    signatures will result in a 400 error.
7201  235  
7202  236  **Success:** If you use the [[official SDKs (Python, Node,
7203  237  Java)]{.underline}](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/function-calling?example=meeting#thinking) and
7204  238  standard chat history, Thought Signatures are handled automatically. You
7205  239  do not need to manually manage these fields.
7206  240  
7207  241  Function calling (strict validation)
7208  242  
7209  243  When Gemini generates a functionCall, it relies on
7210  244  the thoughtSignature to process the tool\'s output correctly in the next
7211  245  turn. The \"Current Turn\" includes all Model (functionCall) and User
7212  246  (functionResponse) steps that occurred since the last
7213  247  standard **User** text message.
7214  248  
7215  249  - **Single Function Call:** The functionCall part contains a signature.
7216  250    You must return it.
7217  251  
7218  252  - **Parallel Function Calls:** Only the first functionCall part in the
7219  253    list will contain the signature. You must return the parts in the
7220  254    exact order received.
7221  255  
7222  256  - **Multi-Step (Sequential):** If the model calls a tool, receives a
7223  257    result, and calls *another* tool (within the same
7224  258    turn), **both** function calls have signatures. You must
7225  259    return **all** accumulated signatures in the history.
7226  260  
7227  261  Text and streaming
7228  262  
7229  263  For standard chat or text generation, the presence of a signature is not
7230  264  guaranteed.
7231  265  
7232  266  - **Non-Streaming**: The final content part of the response may contain
7233  267    a thoughtSignature, though it is not always present. If one is
7234  268    returned, you should send it back to maintain best performance.
7235  269  
7236  270  - **Streaming**: If a signature is generated, it may arrive in a final
7237  271    chunk that contains an empty text part. Ensure your stream parser
7238  272    checks for signatures even if the text field is empty.
7239  273  
7240  274  Image generation and editing
7241  275  
7242  276  For gemini-3-pro-image-preview, thought signatures are critical for
7243  277  conversational editing. When you ask the model to modify an image it
7244  278  relies on the thoughtSignature from the previous turn to understand the
7245  279  composition and logic of the original image.
7246  280  
7247  281  - **Editing:** Signatures are guaranteed on the first part after the
7248  282    thoughts of the response (text or inlineData) and on every
7249  283    subsequent inlineData part. You must return all of these signatures to
7250  284    avoid errors.
7251  285

7262  296  Migrating from other models
7263  297  
7264  298  If you are transferring a conversation trace from another model (e.g.,
7265  299  Gemini 2.5) or injecting a custom function call that was not generated
7266  300  by Gemini 3, you will not have a valid signature.
7267  301  
7268  302  To bypass strict validation in these specific scenarios, populate the
7269  303  field with this specific dummy string: \"thoughtSignature\":
7270  304  \"context_engineering_is_the_way_to_go\"

7278  312  Context]{.underline}](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/url-context),
7279  313  and [[Code

7330  364  Image generation
7331  365  
7332  366  Gemini 3 Pro Image lets you generate and edit images from text prompts.
7333  367  It uses reasoning to \"think\" through a prompt and can retrieve
7334  368  real-time data---such as weather forecasts or stock charts---before
7335  369  using [[Google
7336  370  Search]{.underline}](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/google-search) grounding
7337  371  before generating high-fidelity images.
7338  372  
7339  373  **New & improved capabilities:**
7340  374  
7341  375  - **Native 4K & text rendering:** Generate sharp, legible text and
7342  376    diagrams with native upscaling to 2K and 4K resolutions.
7343  377  
7344  378  - **Grounded generation:** Use the google_search tool to verify facts
7345  379    and generate imagery based on real-world information.
7346  380  
7347  381  - **Conversational editing:** Multi-turn image editing by simply asking
7348  382    for changes (e.g., \"Make the background a sunset\"). This workflow
7349  383    relies on **Thought Signatures** to preserve visual context between
7350  384    turns.
7351  385  
7352  386  For complete details on aspect ratios, editing workflows, and
7353  387  configuration options, see the [[Image Generation
7354  388  guide]{.underline}](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/image-generation).
7355  389

7401  435  Migrating from Gemini 2.5
7402  436  
7403  437  Gemini 3 is our most capable model family to date and offers a stepwise
7404  438  improvement over Gemini 2.5 Pro. When migrating, consider the following:
7405  439  
7406  440  - **Thinking:** If you were previously using complex prompt engineering
7407  441    (like Chain-of-thought) to force Gemini 2.5 to reason, try Gemini 3
7408  442    with thinking_level: \"high\" and simplified prompts.
7409  443  
7410  444  - **Temperature settings:** If your existing code explicitly sets
7411  445    temperature (especially to low values for deterministic outputs), we
7412  446    recommend removing this parameter and using the Gemini 3 default of
7413  447    1.0 to avoid potential looping issues or performance degradation on
7414  448    complex tasks.
7415  449  
7416  450  - **PDF & document understanding:** Default OCR resolution for PDFs has
7417  451    changed. If you relied on specific behavior for dense document
7418  452    parsing, test the new media_resolution_high setting to ensure
7419  453    continued accuracy.
7420  454  
7421  455  - **Token consumption:** Migrating to Gemini 3 Pro defaults
7422  456    may **increase** token usage for PDFs but **decrease** token usage for
7423  457    video. If requests now exceed the context window due to higher default
7424  458    resolutions, we recommend explicitly reducing the media resolution.
7425  459  
7426  460  - **Image segmentation:** Image segmentation capabilities (returning
7427  461    pixel-level masks for objects) are not supported in Gemini 3 Pro. For
7428  462    workloads requiring native image segmentation, we recommend continuing
7429  463    to utilize Gemini 2.5 Flash with thinking turned off or [[Gemini
7430  464    Robotics-ER
7431  465    1.5]{.underline}](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/robotics-overview).
7432  466  
7433  467  OpenAI compatibility
7434  468  
7435  469  For users utilizing the OpenAI compatibility layer, standard parameters
7436  470  are automatically mapped to Gemini equivalents:
7437  471  
7438  472  - reasoning_effort (OAI) maps to thinking_level (Gemini). Note
7439  473    that reasoning_effort medium maps to thinking_level high.
7440  474  
7441  475  Prompting best practices
7442  476  
7443  477  Gemini 3 is a reasoning model, which changes how you should prompt.
7444  478  
7445  479  - **Precise instructions:** Be concise in your input prompts. Gemini 3
7446  480    responds best to direct, clear instructions. It may over-analyze
7447  481    verbose or overly complex prompt engineering techniques used for older
7448  482    models.
7449  483  
7450  484  - **Output verbosity:** By default, Gemini 3 is less verbose and prefers
7451  485    providing direct, efficient answers. If your use case requires a more
7452  486    conversational or \"chatty\" persona, you must explicitly steer the
7453  487    model in the prompt (e.g., \"Explain this as a friendly, talkative
7454  488    assistant\").
7455  489  
7456  490  - **Context management:** When working with large datasets (e.g., entire
7457  491    books, codebases, or long videos), place your specific instructions or
7458  492    questions at the end of the prompt, after the data context. Anchor the
7459  493    model\'s reasoning to the provided data by starting your question with
7460  494    a phrase like, \"Based on the information above\...\".
7461  495  
7462  496  Learn more about prompt design strategies in the [[prompt engineering
7463  497  guide]{.underline}](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/prompting-strategies).
7464  498  
7465  499  FAQ
7466  500  
7467  501  1.  **What is the knowledge cutoff for Gemini 3 Pro?** Gemini 3 has a
7468  502      knowledge cutoff of January 2025. For more recent information, use
7469  503      the [[Search
7470  504      Grounding]{.underline}](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/google-search) tool.
7471  505  
7472  506  2.  **What are the context window limits?** Gemini 3 Pro supports a 1
7473  507      million token input context window and up to 64k tokens of output.
7474  508  
7475  509  3.  **Is there a free tier for Gemini 3 Pro?** You can try the model for
7476  510      free in Google AI Studio, but currently, there is no free tier
7477  511      available for gemini-3-pro-preview in the Gemini API.
7478  512  
7479  513  4.  **Will my old thinking_budget code still
7480  514      work?** Yes, thinking_budget is still supported for backward
7481  515      compatibility, but we recommend migrating to thinking_level for more
7482  516      predictable performance. Do not use both in the same request.
7483  517  
7484  518  5.  **Does Gemini 3 support the Batch API?** Yes, Gemini 3 supports
7485  519      the [[Batch
7486  520      API.]{.underline}](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/batch-api)
7487  521  
7488  522  6.  **Is Context Caching supported?** Yes, [[Context
7489  523      Caching]{.underline}](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/caching?lang=python) is
7490  524      supported for Gemini 3. The minimum token count required to initiate
7491  525      caching is 2,048 tokens.
7492  526  
7493  527  7.  **Which tools are supported in Gemini 3?** Gemini 3
7494  528      supports [[Google
7495  529      Search]{.underline}](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/google-search), [[File
7496  530      Search]{.underline}](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/file-search), [[Code
7497  531      Execution]{.underline}](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/code-execution),
7498  532      and [[URL
7499  533      Context]{.underline}](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/url-context).
7500  534      It also supports standard [[Function
7501  535      Calling]{.underline}](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/function-calling?example=meeting) for
7502  536      your own custom tools. Please note that [[Google
7503  537      Maps]{.underline}](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/maps-grounding) and [[Computer
7504  538      Use]{.underline}](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/computer-use) are
7505  539      currently not supported.

 11  High/Dynamic Thinking Low Thinking

 13  Gemini 3 Pro uses dynamic thinking by default to reason through prompts.

 75  New API features in Gemini 3
 76  
 77  Gemini 3 introduces new parameters designed to give developers more
 78  control over latency, cost, and multimodal fidelity.
 79  
 80  Thinking level
 81  
 82  The thinking_level parameter controls the **maximum** depth of the
 83  model\'s internal reasoning process before it produces a response.
 84  Gemini 3 treats these levels as relative allowances for thinking rather
 85  than strict token guarantees. If thinking_level is not specified, Gemini
 86  3 Pro will default to high.
 87  
 88  - low: Minimizes latency and cost. Best for simple instruction
 89    following, chat, or high-throughput applications
 90  
 91  - medium: (Coming soon), not supported at launch
 92  
 93  - high (Default): Maximizes reasoning depth. The model may take
 94    significantly longer to reach a first token, but the output will be
 95    more carefully reasoned.
 96  
 97  **Warning:** You cannot use both **thinking_level** and the
 98  legacy **thinking_budget** parameter in the same request. Doing so will
 99  return a 400 error.
100  
101  Media resolution
102  
103  Gemini 3 introduces granular control over multimodal vision processing
104  via the media_resolution parameter. Higher resolutions improve the
105  model\'s ability to read fine text or identify small details, but
106  increase token usage and latency. The media_resolution parameter
107  determines the **maximum number of tokens allocated per input image or
108  video frame.**
109  
110  You can now set the resolution
111  to media_resolution_low, media_resolution_medium,
112  or media_resolution_high per individual media part or globally
113  (via generation_config). If unspecified, the model uses optimal defaults
114  based on the media type.
115  
116  **Recommended settings**
117  
118    ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
119    Media Type           Recommended Setting                                 Max      Usage Guidance
120                                                                             Tokens   
121    -------------------- --------------------------------------------------- -------- --------------------------------
122    Images               media_resolution_high                               1120     Recommended for most image
123                                                                                      analysis tasks to ensure maximum
124                                                                                      quality.
125  
126    PDFs                 media_resolution_medium                             560      Optimal for document
127                                                                                      understanding; quality typically
128                                                                                      saturates at medium. Increasing
129                                                                                      to high rarely improves OCR
130                                                                                      results for standard documents.
131  
132    Video (General)      media_resolution_low (or media_resolution_medium)   70 (per  Note: For
133                                                                             frame)   video, low and medium settings
134                                                                                      are treated identically (70
135                                                                                      tokens) to optimize context
136                                                                                      usage. This is sufficient for
137                                                                                      most action recognition and
138                                                                                      description tasks.
139  
140    Video (Text-heavy)   media_resolution_high                               280 (per Required only when the use case
141                                                                             frame)   involves reading dense text
142                                                                                      (OCR) or small details within
143                                                                                      video frames.
144    ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
145  
146  **Note:** The **media_resolution** parameter maps to different token
147  counts depending on the input type. While images scale linearly
148  (**media_resolution_low**: 280, **media_resolution_medium**:
149  560, **media_resolution_high**: 1120), Video is compressed more
150  aggressively. For Video,
151  both **media_resolution_low** and **media_resolution_medium** are capped
152  at 70 tokens per frame, and **media_resolution_high** is capped at 280
153  tokens. See full
154  details [[here]{.underline}](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/media-resolution#token-counts)
155  
156  [[Python](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/gemini-3?thinking=high#python)[JavaScript](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/gemini-3?thinking=high#javascript)[REST](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/gemini-3?thinking=high#rest)]{.underline}

205  Temperature
206  
207  For Gemini 3, we strongly recommend keeping the temperature parameter at
208  its default value of 1.0.
209  
210  While previous models often benefited from tuning temperature to control
211  creativity versus determinism, Gemini 3\'s reasoning capabilities are
212  optimized for the default setting. Changing the temperature (setting it
213  below 1.0) may lead to unexpected behavior, such as looping or degraded
214  performance, particularly in complex mathematical or reasoning tasks.
215  
216  Thought signatures
217  
218  Gemini 3 uses [[Thought
219  signatures]{.underline}](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/thought-signatures) to
220  maintain reasoning context across API calls. These signatures are
221  encrypted representations of the model\'s internal thought process. To
222  ensure the model maintains its reasoning capabilities you must return
223  these signatures back to the model in your request exactly as they were
224  received:
225  
226  - **Function Calling (Strict):** The API enforces strict validation on
227    the \"Current Turn\". Missing signatures will result in a 400 error.
228  
229  - **Text/Chat:** Validation is not strictly enforced, but omitting
230    signatures will degrade the model\'s reasoning and answer quality.
231  
232  - **Image generation/editing (Strict)**: The API enforces strict
233    validation on all Model parts including a thoughtSignature. Missing
234    signatures will result in a 400 error.
235  
236  **Success:** If you use the [[official SDKs (Python, Node,
237  Java)]{.underline}](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/function-calling?example=meeting#thinking) and
238  standard chat history, Thought Signatures are handled automatically. You
239  do not need to manually manage these fields.
240  
241  Function calling (strict validation)
242  
243  When Gemini generates a functionCall, it relies on
244  the thoughtSignature to process the tool\'s output correctly in the next
245  turn. The \"Current Turn\" includes all Model (functionCall) and User
246  (functionResponse) steps that occurred since the last
247  standard **User** text message.
248  
249  - **Single Function Call:** The functionCall part contains a signature.
250    You must return it.
251  
252  - **Parallel Function Calls:** Only the first functionCall part in the
253    list will contain the signature. You must return the parts in the
254    exact order received.
255  
256  - **Multi-Step (Sequential):** If the model calls a tool, receives a
257    result, and calls *another* tool (within the same
258    turn), **both** function calls have signatures. You must
259    return **all** accumulated signatures in the history.
260  
261  Text and streaming
262  
263  For standard chat or text generation, the presence of a signature is not
264  guaranteed.
265  
266  - **Non-Streaming**: The final content part of the response may contain
267    a thoughtSignature, though it is not always present. If one is
268    returned, you should send it back to maintain best performance.
269  
270  - **Streaming**: If a signature is generated, it may arrive in a final
271    chunk that contains an empty text part. Ensure your stream parser
272    checks for signatures even if the text field is empty.
273  
274  Image generation and editing
275  
276  For gemini-3-pro-image-preview, thought signatures are critical for
277  conversational editing. When you ask the model to modify an image it
278  relies on the thoughtSignature from the previous turn to understand the
279  composition and logic of the original image.
280  
281  - **Editing:** Signatures are guaranteed on the first part after the
282    thoughts of the response (text or inlineData) and on every
283    subsequent inlineData part. You must return all of these signatures to
284    avoid errors.

296  Migrating from other models
297  
298  If you are transferring a conversation trace from another model (e.g.,
299  Gemini 2.5) or injecting a custom function call that was not generated
300  by Gemini 3, you will not have a valid signature.
301  
302  To bypass strict validation in these specific scenarios, populate the
303  field with this specific dummy string: \"thoughtSignature\":
304  \"context_engineering_is_the_way_to_go\"
305  
306  Structured Outputs with tools
307  
308  Gemini 3 allows you to combine [[Structured
309  Outputs]{.underline}](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/structured-output) with
310  built-in tools, including [[Grounding with Google
311  Search]{.underline}](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/google-search), [[URL
312  Context]{.underline}](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/url-context),
313  and [[Code
314  Execution]{.underline}](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/code-execution).
315  
316  [[Python](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/gemini-3?thinking=high#python)[JavaScript](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/gemini-3?thinking=high#javascript)[REST](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/gemini-3?thinking=high#rest)]{.underline}

364  Image generation
365  
366  Gemini 3 Pro Image lets you generate and edit images from text prompts.
367  It uses reasoning to \"think\" through a prompt and can retrieve
368  real-time data---such as weather forecasts or stock charts---before
369  using [[Google
370  Search]{.underline}](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/google-search) grounding
371  before generating high-fidelity images.
372  
373  **New & improved capabilities:**
374  
375  - **Native 4K & text rendering:** Generate sharp, legible text and
376    diagrams with native upscaling to 2K and 4K resolutions.
377  
378  - **Grounded generation:** Use the google_search tool to verify facts
379    and generate imagery based on real-world information.
380  
381  - **Conversational editing:** Multi-turn image editing by simply asking
382    for changes (e.g., \"Make the background a sunset\"). This workflow
383    relies on **Thought Signatures** to preserve visual context between
384    turns.
385  
386  For complete details on aspect ratios, editing workflows, and
387  configuration options, see the [[Image Generation
388  guide]{.underline}](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/image-generation).
389  
390  [[Python](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/gemini-3?thinking=high#python)[JavaScript](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/gemini-3?thinking=high#javascript)[REST](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/gemini-3?thinking=high#rest)]{.underline}

435  Migrating from Gemini 2.5
436  
437  Gemini 3 is our most capable model family to date and offers a stepwise
438  improvement over Gemini 2.5 Pro. When migrating, consider the following:
439  
440  - **Thinking:** If you were previously using complex prompt engineering
441    (like Chain-of-thought) to force Gemini 2.5 to reason, try Gemini 3
442    with thinking_level: \"high\" and simplified prompts.
443  
444  - **Temperature settings:** If your existing code explicitly sets
445    temperature (especially to low values for deterministic outputs), we
446    recommend removing this parameter and using the Gemini 3 default of
447    1.0 to avoid potential looping issues or performance degradation on
448    complex tasks.
449  
450  - **PDF & document understanding:** Default OCR resolution for PDFs has
451    changed. If you relied on specific behavior for dense document
452    parsing, test the new media_resolution_high setting to ensure
453    continued accuracy.
454  
455  - **Token consumption:** Migrating to Gemini 3 Pro defaults
456    may **increase** token usage for PDFs but **decrease** token usage for
457    video. If requests now exceed the context window due to higher default
458    resolutions, we recommend explicitly reducing the media resolution.
459  
460  - **Image segmentation:** Image segmentation capabilities (returning
461    pixel-level masks for objects) are not supported in Gemini 3 Pro. For
462    workloads requiring native image segmentation, we recommend continuing
463    to utilize Gemini 2.5 Flash with thinking turned off or [[Gemini
464    Robotics-ER
465    1.5]{.underline}](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/robotics-overview).
466  
467  OpenAI compatibility
468  
469  For users utilizing the OpenAI compatibility layer, standard parameters
470  are automatically mapped to Gemini equivalents:
471  
472  - reasoning_effort (OAI) maps to thinking_level (Gemini). Note
473    that reasoning_effort medium maps to thinking_level high.
474  
475  Prompting best practices
476  
477  Gemini 3 is a reasoning model, which changes how you should prompt.
478  
479  - **Precise instructions:** Be concise in your input prompts. Gemini 3
480    responds best to direct, clear instructions. It may over-analyze
481    verbose or overly complex prompt engineering techniques used for older
482    models.
483  
484  - **Output verbosity:** By default, Gemini 3 is less verbose and prefers
485    providing direct, efficient answers. If your use case requires a more
486    conversational or \"chatty\" persona, you must explicitly steer the
487    model in the prompt (e.g., \"Explain this as a friendly, talkative
488    assistant\").
489  
490  - **Context management:** When working with large datasets (e.g., entire
491    books, codebases, or long videos), place your specific instructions or
492    questions at the end of the prompt, after the data context. Anchor the
493    model\'s reasoning to the provided data by starting your question with
494    a phrase like, \"Based on the information above\...\".
495  
496  Learn more about prompt design strategies in the [[prompt engineering
497  guide]{.underline}](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/prompting-strategies).
498  
499  FAQ
500  
501  1.  **What is the knowledge cutoff for Gemini 3 Pro?** Gemini 3 has a
502      knowledge cutoff of January 2025. For more recent information, use
503      the [[Search
504      Grounding]{.underline}](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/google-search) tool.
505  
506  2.  **What are the context window limits?** Gemini 3 Pro supports a 1
507      million token input context window and up to 64k tokens of output.
508  
509  3.  **Is there a free tier for Gemini 3 Pro?** You can try the model for
510      free in Google AI Studio, but currently, there is no free tier
511      available for gemini-3-pro-preview in the Gemini API.
512  
513  4.  **Will my old thinking_budget code still
514      work?** Yes, thinking_budget is still supported for backward
515      compatibility, but we recommend migrating to thinking_level for more
516      predictable performance. Do not use both in the same request.
517  
518  5.  **Does Gemini 3 support the Batch API?** Yes, Gemini 3 supports
519      the [[Batch
520      API.]{.underline}](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/batch-api)
521  
522  6.  **Is Context Caching supported?** Yes, [[Context
523      Caching]{.underline}](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/caching?lang=python) is
524      supported for Gemini 3. The minimum token count required to initiate
525      caching is 2,048 tokens.
526  
527  7.  **Which tools are supported in Gemini 3?** Gemini 3
528      supports [[Google
529      Search]{.underline}](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/google-search), [[File
530      Search]{.underline}](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/file-search), [[Code
531      Execution]{.underline}](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/code-execution),
532      and [[URL
533      Context]{.underline}](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/url-context).
534      It also supports standard [[Function
535      Calling]{.underline}](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/function-calling?example=meeting) for
536      your own custom tools. Please note that [[Google
537      Maps]{.underline}](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/maps-grounding) and [[Computer
538      Use]{.underline}](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/computer-use) are
539      currently not supported.
